entries.body: Coverage Labs — Palisade Independent Examination COVERAGE / LABS INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATION ENVIRONMENT V0.1.4 · PALISADE EXAM / LOCAL ← HOME FIELD EXAMINATION / CASE PA-014 / FICTIONAL SIMULATION EVERY REGION. WITHIN REACH? Palisade Civic Health Group says its regional network puts care within reach wherever members live. Investigate the claim, the organisations behind it and the records that describe how the route actually works. OPEN THE ASSIGNMENT ↘ EXAM CONDITIONS / NO GUIDED HINTS / NO SUGGESTED FINDINGS / YOUR EVIDENCE. YOUR CONCLUSIONS. EXAM ROUTE / PA-014 00 Assignment 01 Organisation 02 Claims 03 Source desk 04 Evidence trail 05 Findings 06 Final report 0 of 7 work areas reviewed SAVE WORK EXPORT NOTES 00 / THE BRIEF Establish what “within reach” means. START HERE Commission: Prepare an independent investigative dossier on Palisade Civic Health Group and its “Every Region, Within Reach” public promise. Your central question What does Palisade's regional access claim actually establish, who is responsible for each part of the service, and what can the available records prove about practical access? You are not being asked to prove that Palisade is good or bad. You are being asked to establish what is supported, what is qualified or contradicted, what remains unknown, and how confident you can reasonably be. Scope: group structure, insurance-provider responsibility, delegated route operations, directory metrics, provider capacity, referral handling and the limits of the available evidence. Deliverable: a concise company profile, entity map, claims register, source assessments, evidence matrix, findings with status and confidence, unresolved questions and final report. Your initial investigation plan MARK WORK AREA REVIEWED 01 / ORGANISATION Who is Palisade? ENTITY MAPPING Establish the legal entities and operational relationships. Distinguish parent ownership, insurance responsibility, delegated services and independent providers. Use the registry, group report, policy schedule and service agreement as relevant. Entity map and relationships Responsibility boundaries MARK WORK AREA REVIEWED 02 / CLAIMS What is being claimed? DECONSTRUCTION Identify the material public and implied claims. Convert broad language into propositions that could be tested. Do not treat a headline, metric or corporate definition as self-validating. Claims register Operational definitions and denominators MARK WORK AREA REVIEWED 03 / SOURCE DESK Open the records. 11 DOCUMENTS Use the company website, wiki, research desk, institutional pages and original documents. Evaluate each source for authority, proximity to the event, purpose, date, scope, method and limitations. PALISADE WEBSITE ↗ COMPANY WIKI ↗ RESEARCH DESK ↗ ATLAS REGISTRY ↗ WAYPOINT AUDIT OFFICE ↗ Primary source shelf PAL-SRC-001 Palisade Civic Health Group — Annual Review 2025 2026-02-18 · Parent company PAL-SRC-002 Atlas Registry — Certified Entity Extract 26-0441 2026-03-04 · Corporate registry PAL-SRC-003 Palisade Zorgverzekering — Policy and Responsibility Schedule 2027 2026-09-12 · Insurance provider PAL-SRC-004 Intra-group Service Agreement — Route Operations 2025-11-28 · Contract PAL-SRC-005 Regional Route Directory — Methodology and Snapshot Q3 2026 2026-10-03 · Methodology / dataset note PAL-SRC-006 Route Services — Q3 2026 Operational Dashboard 2026-10-14 · Operational dashboard PAL-SRC-007 North Coast Provider Notice and Capacity Bulletin 2026-08-21 · Provider-originated notice PAL-SRC-008 Member Route Case Sample — Redacted Training Extract 2026-09-30 · Case sample PAL-SRC-009 Regional Access Review — Waypoint Audit Office 2026-11-02 · Independent oversight review PAL-SRC-010 Palisade Public Statement — “Every Region, Within Reach” 2026-10-20 · Public statement PAL-SRC-011 Board Risk Committee Minutes — Access Metrics 2026-10-28 · Governance record Ownership, capital and related-party map Commercial incentives and competing motives Discriminating evidence and falsifiers Related institutional source rooms Open the institutions directory ↗ · Search shareholdings in VINDR ↗ · Search energy and infrastructure records ↗ Source evaluation notes MARK WORK AREA REVIEWED 04 / EVIDENCE TRAIL Connect the record. TRACEABILITY Build a claim-by-claim evidence trail. Identify supporting, contradictory and qualifying material. Distinguish what a document directly records from what you infer by combining records. Evidence matrix Chronology and contradictions Direct evidence versus inference MARK WORK AREA REVIEWED 05 / FINDINGS What can you conclude? STATUS ≠ CONFIDENCE Assess each material claim. Use the project's evidence-status vocabulary and make a separate confidence judgement. Explain the reasons and identify unresolved questions. Do not force a conclusion where the record is incomplete. Findings and evidence status Confidence assessment Unresolved questions and further evidence MARK WORK AREA REVIEWED 06 / FINAL REPORT Write the investigation. YOUR CONCLUSIONS Prepare a concise, readable report. State the scope and date, identify the relevant organisations, explain the important findings, cite the evidence and disclose limitations. Avoid stronger language than the evidence supports. Company profile and entity summary Executive summary and principal findings Evidence citations Limitations and next steps Final self-check I distinguished the group, insurer and service company. I tested claims against original records. I assessed source relevance and limitations. I recorded supporting and contradictory evidence. I separated evidence status from confidence. I preserved unknowns and disclosed limitations. This workspace records your own work locally in this browser. It does not grade the investigation, verify citations or submit anything to another person. MARK WORK AREA REVIEWED MARK EXAM WORK COMPLETE SAVE FINAL WORK RETURN TO COVERAGE LABS HOME → PALISADE / CASE PA-014 / FICTIONAL TRAINING MATERIAL V0.1.4 · INDEPENDENT EXAM EXPERIENCE

entries.title: BRAND_IDENTITIES.md
entries.body:
# Expanded fictional brand identities

> Every brand and organisation in this file is invented.

| Brand | Experience | Visual language | Research discovery style |
|---|---|---|---|
| Noordlicht Zorg | Y2K cyber-goth / Windows 7 Aero | Electric pink, baby pink, lilac glass, beveled windows, taskbar, chaotic desktop icons | Desktop archaeology: member meeting records, supplier files, registry evidence and archive history |
| Rivierzorg Direct | Liquid glass / PS3 XMB-inspired console | Turquoise, marine blue, soft glass, horizontal nav rail, optional dark mode, fluid restrained motion | Systems investigation: API map, event codes, data dictionary, service reliability and metric definitions |
| Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg | Windows 8 Metro / family archive | Warm rust, brown-red, clay, parchment, flat tiles and simple transitions | Household and cooperative research: person categories, family eligibility, member voting and regional partner ledgers |
| Frequency Health Group | 2002 digital cable guide / sixth-generation console dashboard | Electric blue, ultraviolet, hot magenta, acid lime, chrome-like borders, CRT scanline texture and channel tiles | Service-metric investigation: interaction closure, member outcomes, legal entities and provider-slot visibility |

The company worlds use different navigation patterns and visual metaphors. Their research records still share stable evidence standards, so the user learns one methodology while encountering different source types and discovery paths.

entries.title: COMPARISON.md
entries.body:
# Three-insurer comparison - fictional 2027

> All companies, policies, legal identities, prices, provider networks, benefits and statistics are invented. This is a research-practice scenario only.

| Dimension | Noordlicht Zorg | Rivierzorg Direct | Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Parent group | Noordlicht Holding U.A. | Riviergroep N.V. | Kompas Gezondheid Groep U.A. |
| Legal insurer | Noordlicht Zorgverzekeraar N.V. | Rivierzorg Verzekeringen N.V. | Kompas Zorgverzekeraar U.A. |
| Basic policy | Noordlicht Basis | Rivier Basis Select | Kompas Ruime Keuze |
| Monthly basic premium | €159.75 | €145.50 | €168.90 |
| Annual basic premium | €1,917.00 | €1,746.00 | €2,026.80 |
| Policy type | Naturapolis | Budget naturapolis | Ruime naturapolis |
| Non-contracted reimbursement | 70% tariff basis, with caps | 60% tariff basis, with additional caps | 85% tariff basis, subject to terms |
| Hospital network headline | 92% of hospital organisations | 78% of hospital addresses marked active | 95% of hospital organisations with any active agreement |
| Mental healthcare | National network / standard triage | Digital-first, thinner face-to-face network | Dedicated navigation and wait-list mediation |
| Gender-affirming care | Three-region Halo route | External referral; no dedicated pathway | Partner centres and named navigator |
| Women's / pelvic health | Midwifery, gynaecology, pelvic physio subject to terms | Standard network; fewer rural clinics | Stronger pelvic-health route in core provinces |
| Disability / rehabilitation | Complex-care coordinator after referral | Digital aids process; limited named case management | Named case manager for eligible complex cases |
| Physiotherapy | 9 sessions in Extra | 6 sessions in Start | 12 sessions in Plus |
| Dental | 75% up to €350 in Extra | 75% up to €250 in Start | 80% up to €500 in Plus |
| Complaint/service headline | 3.8 per 1,000 | 5.6 per 1,000 | 3.1 per 1,000 |

## Do not rank the headline percentages

The three hospital network figures use different units and definitions: Noordlicht counts hospital organisations with a general agreement; Rivierzorg counts addresses marked ACTIVE in a directory snapshot; Kompas counts organisations with any active agreement. None measures all specialties, appointment capacity, waiting time or care access for a specific patient.

The complaint figures are also not comparable: Noordlicht counts formally registered complaints and excludes several early contacts; Rivierzorg counts tagged support tickets per active digital account; Kompas counts upheld formal complaints using year-end insured persons. Rivierzorg's separate claims-speed metric covers only routine machine-readable app claims and excludes multiple categories.

## Product-level comparison matters

The monthly basic premium does not include supplementary packages. Annual limits, waiting periods, prior approval, dental exclusions, treatment codes and actual provider contracts matter. The assumed deductible in this simulation is a scenario parameter only.

## Research journeys

- Noordlicht: Y2K Aero desktop archaeology.
- Rivierzorg: liquid-glass platform and network telemetry.
- Kompas: Metro tiles, family eligibility and cooperative governance.

## No overall winner

There is no score or universal winner. Personal location, treatment needs, policy version, provider contracts, out-of-pocket tolerance and practical access change the suitability analysis.

# FREQUENCY — Company Entry

**Identity:** FREQUENCY Health Group (fictional)
**Design era:** 2002 digital cable guide / sixth-generation console dashboard.
**Case:** FE-013 — One Call, One Answer?

Start with the [public website](website/index.html), inspect the [wiki](wiki/index.html), then open the [research desk](research/desk.html). The complete worked example is available from the Coverage Labs learner home.

All entities, records, metrics, people and publications are invented for Coverage Labs.

## Background systems note

**Background workflow platform (fictional):** Frequency uses a separate GoedGeregeld GG Flow tenant for interaction queues and status events. Frequency defines its own reporting rules; a platform status is not automatically a member-level outcome.

entries.title: Subscriber retention and service automation investment note
entries.body: Subscriber retention and service automation investment note FICTIONAL INTERNAL SOURCE / FRQ-2026-11 Subscriber retention and service automation investment note Publication date: 2026-11-14 · Strategy and finance committee extract Frequency management proposes a multi-year investment in automated member-service workflows and media-partner account management. The business case links lower support cost per subscriber to retention of bundled media and care subscriptions. The paper is authored by management and does not establish that any individual case was mishandled. Limitations: this is a management-authored proposal, not evidence of implementation or member-level outcomes.

entries.body:
FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  FREQUENCY / DOCUMENT ARCHIVE

  Annual Signal Report 2026
  Frequency Health Group — corporate publication



  Document ID: FREQ-SRC-001
  Classification: Fictional simulation material
  Issue date: 14 February 2027
  Publisher: Frequency Health Group

  This document is invented for investigative training. It is not a real company record, legal filing,
  provider report or publication.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                          01
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  A connected promise
  Frequency Health Group describes itself as a connected care organisation. Its 2026 annual signal report says that
  members should experience “one call, one answer” across the group. The group reports that 88% of eligible service
  contacts were resolved at first contact during the final quarter of 2026.

  Headline metric: 88% first-contact resolution (FCR), Q4 2026. The report does not define “resolved” in
  the headline section.

  Group structure as presented
   Entity                                                       Role described by group

   Frequency Health Group U.A.                                  Parent cooperative and group strategy

   Frequency Zorg N.V.                                          Insurance provider and policy decision entity

   Frequency Connect B.V.                                       Member contact centre and service operations

   Frequency Network B.V.                                       Provider directory and network coordination


  The report says the shared “Frequency” brand creates a single member experience. It does not state that the entities are
  one legal person.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                              02
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Performance narrative
  The report highlights a 12-point increase in FCR compared with the first quarter of 2026. It attributes the improvement to a
  new routing platform called TUNE and a revised “resolve before transfer” workflow.

   Quarter                                                        Reported FCR

   Q1 2026                                                        76%

   Q2 2026                                                        81%

   Q3 2026                                                        85%

   Q4 2026                                                        88%


  The report does not include a contact-level dataset, a definition of eligible contacts, a repeat-contact window or a
  reconciliation between call records and case-management records.

  Other public claims
  • 92% of listed network locations display an appointment slot within 14 calendar days.

  • Every member has one named route into the Frequency service system.

  • The report describes the network as “continuously monitored”.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                                  03
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Governance note
  The board states that Frequency Connect operates the first-line service desk under an intra-group services agreement.
  Frequency Zorg retains policy interpretation, coverage decisions and formal complaint determinations. Frequency Network
  maintains the provider directory and receives updates from participating providers.

  The report does not append the services agreement, the network data specification or the board-approved metric
  definitions.

  Investigative caution: this document establishes what the group publicly says. It is not independent
  verification of the claims.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                             04

FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  FREQUENCY / DOCUMENT ARCHIVE

  Member Services Agreement — Extract
  Frequency Zorg N.V. and Frequency Connect B.V. — executed fictional agreement



  Document ID: FREQ-SRC-003
  Classification: Fictional simulation material
  Issue date: 14 February 2027
  Publisher: Frequency Zorg N.V. and Frequency Connect B.V.

  This document is invented for investigative training. It is not a real company record, legal filing,
  provider report or publication.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                          01
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Purpose and parties
  Agreement dated 1 July 2026 between Frequency Zorg N.V. (“Provider”) and Frequency Connect B.V. (“Service
  Operator”). Frequency Connect supplies first-line member contact, identity verification, document intake, triage and case
  routing.

  Clause 2 — Allocation of responsibility
  • The Provider retains responsibility for policy interpretation, benefit eligibility, coverage decisions and formal complaint
  determinations.

  • The Service Operator may provide scripted factual information but must route disputed coverage questions to the
  Provider.

  • The Service Operator may mark a contact interaction complete after providing information, transferring the member or
  creating a follow-up task.

  The agreement distinguishes completion of a contact interaction from resolution of the member’s
  underlying issue.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                                   02
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Clause 4 — Case handling
  The Service Operator must create a case identifier when a contact requires work beyond the initial interaction. A case may
  be closed when a response is sent, when a referral is accepted by a receiving team, or when the member is advised to
  contact another organisation.

  The Provider must determine formal complaints and coverage disputes. The Service Operator may receive and route
  complaint submissions but may not issue a final determination.

  Clause 7 — Reporting
  Monthly service reporting is based on interaction records supplied by the Service Operator. The Provider may request
  case-level reconciliation, but this extract contains no evidence that such reconciliation occurred during Q4 2026.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                                03
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Missing schedules
  The signed agreement refers to Schedule A (service definitions), Schedule C (escalation matrix), Schedule D (quality
  assurance) and Schedule F (data exchange). None is included in this extract.

  The extract establishes the division of specified contractual duties between the two named parties. It does not establish
  whether all operational practices complied with the agreement.

  Do not treat a contractual allocation as proof of actual performance. Seek operational records and the
  missing schedules.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                               04

entries.title: FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD
entries.body:
FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  FREQUENCY / DOCUMENT ARCHIVE

  TUNE KPI Methodology v3.2
  Frequency Connect B.V. — internal metric specification



  Document ID: FREQ-SRC-004
  Classification: Fictional simulation material
  Issue date: 14 February 2027
  Publisher: Frequency Connect B.V.

  This document is invented for investigative training. It is not a real company record, legal filing,
  provider report or publication.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                          01
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Metric definition
  First-contact resolution (FCR) is calculated as the number of eligible interaction records marked “resolved” before the
  interaction is closed, divided by all eligible interaction records in the reporting period.

  FCR = eligible interaction records with status RESOLVED at closure ÷ all eligible interaction records ×
  100.

  Eligibility rules
  • Inbound telephone and live-chat interactions with a valid interaction ID are included.

  • Outbound callbacks, provider-portal messages and contacts without a generated interaction ID are excluded.

  • A transfer is not automatically excluded. If the agent selects RESOLVED before transfer, the interaction counts as
  resolved.

  • The metric does not link subsequent contacts by the same member unless they share the original interaction ID.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                             02
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Closure codes
   Code                                    Meaning in TUNE                               FCR treatment

   RESOLVED                                Agent selected a closure outcome indicating   Numerator
                                           an answer or next step was provided

   REFERRED                                Contact transferred to another team or        Denominator only
                                           external provider

   FOLLOW-UP                               A task or callback was created                Denominator only

   ABANDONED                               Member disconnected before handling           Excluded when no agent interaction is
                                                                                         recorded


  A RESOLVED code may be used when an answer is given, a transfer is accepted, or a follow-up route is explained. It
  does not require confirmation that the member’s underlying issue was solved.

  Quality assurance
  The methodology specifies a monthly sample review of 30 interactions. The sample checks whether the selected closure
  code is consistent with the interaction notes; it does not check whether the member’s issue was later resolved.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                                  03
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Version history and limits
  Version 3.2 approved 4 October 2026. It replaced version 3.1, which used a 48-hour repeat-contact matching rule. Version
  3.2 removed that rule because interaction IDs were not consistently shared across channels.

  The specification contains no member-level outcome measure, no 7-day or 30-day repeat-contact rate, and no case-level
  closure reconciliation.

  This source explains what the 88% metric measures. It cannot establish whether the underlying
  records were entered accurately.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                              04

  Frequency Quality Office — fictional internal sample



  Document ID: FREQ-SRC-006
  Classification: Fictional simulation material
  Issue date: 14 February 2027
  Publisher: Frequency Quality Office

  This document is invented for investigative training. It is not a real company record, legal filing,
  provider report or publication.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                          01
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Review purpose
  The Quality Office reviewed 40 member journeys selected from a complaint follow-up queue in January 2027. The review
  linked interactions by member reference and issue description where possible.

   Review result                              Cases                                Notes

   Same issue contacted again within 7 days   17                                   New interaction ID in 14 cases

   Transferred to another team                12                                   8 later contacts in sample

   Follow-up task created                     9                                    6 remained open after 5 working days

   No repeat contact found in sample window   6                                    Absence of repeat contact is not proof of
                                                                                   resolution


  The categories overlap: a case may have been transferred and later contacted again. The counts are descriptive of the
  selected sample only.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                                02
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Selected journey extracts
   Journey                                First contact                            Subsequent record

   Q-014                                  Agent selected RESOLVED; member asked    Provider portal message 2 days later;
                                          about reimbursement                      separate case ID

   Q-021                                  Agent selected RESOLVED after transfer   Receiving team requested missing
                                          acceptance                               documents 4 days later

   Q-028                                  Agent selected FOLLOW-UP                 Task remained open at review date

   Q-033                                  Agent selected RESOLVED after giving     Member called provider 3 days later;
                                          provider phone number                    outcome not recorded


  These examples show why a contact closure code and the member’s eventual outcome are different things. They do not
  prove that all or most Frequency interactions fail.

  Limitations

COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                          01
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Public network metric
  The group annual report states that 92% of listed network locations display an appointment slot within 14 calendar days.
  This bulletin explains the network-side snapshot used for the figure.

  The denominator is 1,840 listed location records with a valid weekly data feed. A location counts as “slot visible” when its
  latest feed contains at least one bookable-looking slot within 14 days.

  Important exclusions
  • The feed does not confirm that the slot is still available when a member attempts to book.

  • The feed does not test whether the slot is suitable for the member’s requested treatment.

  • The feed does not include all non-digital booking routes.

  • The report does not measure travel time, waiting-list status after triage, or whether a referral is accepted.

   Locations with incomplete specialty mapping                 203


  Late feeds were retained using the most recent available snapshot. The report does not state how many late feeds were
  more than seven days old.

  The metric establishes visibility of a slot in a data feed. It does not establish that a member can
  actually obtain a suitable appointment within 14 days.

entries.title: FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD
entries.body:
FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  FREQUENCY / DOCUMENT ARCHIVE

  The Queue Is Not the Outcome
  The Signal Desk — independent fictional reporting



  Document ID: FREQ-SRC-009
  Classification: Fictional simulation material
  Issue date: 14 February 2027
  Publisher: The Signal Desk

  This document is invented for investigative training. It is not a real company record, legal filing,
  provider report or publication.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                          01
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  A polished interface, a complicated journey
  The Signal Desk reviewed a small number of anonymised member journeys and the published TUNE methodology. The
  report asks whether “one call, one answer” describes a member outcome or a contact-centre workflow.

  Three of nine interviewed members described being told that their first contact was complete even though they still needed
  to contact a provider, submit documents or wait for a second team. The interviews were recruited through an open call and
  cannot represent all members.

  What the reporting found
  • The TUNE methodology counts some accepted transfers as RESOLVED.

  • The dashboard does not link new interaction IDs to earlier contacts by the same member.

  • The member services agreement permits an interaction to be marked complete after a referral or next-step instruction.

  • The board risk note recognises that the group cannot yet evidence the complete member journey.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                                02
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  Company response
  Frequency Health Group told The Signal Desk that “resolved” is a technical service metric, not a guarantee that every
  underlying healthcare journey ends in one interaction. It said the group is reviewing public language and developing a
  member-journey measure.

  The response was received by email on 9 February 2027. The reporter was not given the underlying member-level dataset
  or the complete board minutes.

  The reporting corroborates the interpretation of the methodology but relies on a small, self-selected
  interview group.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                            03
 FREQUENCY / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD




  What remains unknown
  • The proportion of all member issues requiring more than one contact.

  • Whether the proposed linked repeat-contact metric was implemented.

  • How often a transfer leads to a successful outcome without further member effort.

  • Whether the public claim wording changed after February 2027.

  The Signal Desk concludes that the published 88% figure is a real calculation under a narrow interaction-based definition,
  but should not be presented as proof that 88% of member problems are solved at first contact.




COVERAGE LABS · SIMULATION ONLY                                                                                                04

entries.title: GLOSSARY.md
entries.body:
# Research glossary - expanded

- **Parent group:** Wider corporate group above an operating insurer.
- **Operating insurer / legal insurer:** Legal entity named in the insurance contract and bearing the relevant insurance obligations in this simulation.
- **Brand:** Customer-facing identity; it may differ from the legal entity.
- **Policy:** Product contract for a specified insurance year.
- **Policy year:** The period the product terms apply to; never infer a policy year from a document title alone.
- **Supplementary insurance:** Separate optional product with its own premium, eligibility, annual limits and exclusions.
- **Risk carrier:** Entity bearing the insurance risk; do not infer it solely from a group brand.
- **Service provider / processor:** External organisation performing a service. A service contract does not prove ownership or control.
- **Outsourcing concentration:** Dependency on one or a small number of suppliers for operationally important services.
- **Contracted provider:** Provider contracted for the relevant treatment, location and policy year.
- **Directory status:** Administrative code in a provider export; not necessarily evidence of capacity, appointment availability or quality.
- **Legal entitlement:** What applicable law provides. This simulation does not establish real legal entitlements.
- **Contractual entitlement:** What the fictional policy terms promise.
- **Practical accessibility:** Whether a person can actually obtain care in a location and timeframe.
- **Numerator / denominator:** The count included in a metric and the population or unit it is divided by.
- **Evidence status:** Supported, Partly supported, Disputed, Unknown or Outdated.
- **Confidence:** High, Medium, Low or Unknown confidence in the research interpretation; separate from evidence status.
- **Source register:** Structured record of source IDs, publisher, dates, source type, local file and limitations.
- **Claim register:** Atomic claims linked to sources, evidence status, confidence and rationale.
- **Official-style simulation:** Fictional record designed to resemble a document genre, not a real public authority document.

entries.title: Annual report and reserves note
entries.body: Annual report and reserves note FICTIONAL SOURCE RECORD · MNSE Annual report and reserves note Publication: 2026-11-16 · Record ID: MNSE-SRC-AN-2026 A fictional listed upstream oil and gas company with offshore production interests, pipeline capacity rights and decommissioning liabilities in the northern basin. The board forecasts lower output from mature fields and higher maintenance costs. It has approved a capital plan that prioritises tie-back infrastructure and selective workovers. The plan assumes a stable oil price and continued access to pipeline capacity. Commercial incentive: The company seeks to maintain production cash flow, extend the economic life of mature fields and avoid near-term decommissioning costs. Its incentives include reserve replacement, dividend stability and refinancing access. Those incentives do not establish concealment or improper influence. Limitations: this is a company-authored forecast, not independently verified production data. Training simulation. Not a real-world record. SPONSORED · GOEDGEREGELD Make every workflow visible. entries.title: README.md
entries.body:
# External Sources and Institutional Archives

> **Every organisation, staff member, record, filing, contract, publication and institution in this directory is fictional simulation material.** Nothing here represents a real Dutch government body, regulator, bank, insurer or newsroom. The pages have no real-world legal, financial or regulatory authority.

## Institutional directory

- **Kamerregister voor Ondernemingen (KRO):** fictional company register with corporate identity, filing history, historic trade names and officer records.
- **Dienst voor Belastingen en Registratie (DBR):** fictional filing acknowledgements, provisional assessments and payment-allocation receipts. Receipt is not substantive approval.
- **Nederlands Zorgtoezichtbureau (NZT):** fictional sector-level oversight desk publishing thematic notes, sampling methodology and follow-up questionnaires. Aggregate findings are not company-specific enforcement findings.
- **Noorder Cooperative Bank:** fictional cooperative lender. Its facility summary and later credit-monitoring records provide financing leads, not an audit of service quality. The unnamed concentrated customer remains unidentified in the published extracts.
- **De Zorglijn:** fictional specialist newsroom publishing investigations and explainers about outsourcing, network percentages and the limits of administrative records.
- **Civic Lens:** fictional field-note collective. Its records distinguish registered, correspondence and processing addresses and preserve unresolved internal terminology without inventing definitions.
- **Atlas Registry:** fictional entity index with identifier and alias crosswalks.
- **Waypoint Audit Office:** fictional review office examining provider-directory methods and sampling limitations.
- **The Signal Desk:** fictional document-led newsroom associated with the Frequency worked example.

## Source collection

The `Sources/` directory contains the original institutional extracts plus supplemental records introduced for V0.1.4.1. New PDFs vary in length and evidential purpose; page count is not a proxy for reliability.

| Source ID | Publisher | Purpose | Key limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| NCB-2025-77 | Noorder Cooperative Bank | Receivables facility summary | No complete facility agreement or customer ledger |
| NCB-2026-12 | Noorder Cooperative Bank | Concentration covenant notice | Borrower reports 27.4%; customer is unnamed |
| NCB-2026-31 | Noorder Cooperative Bank | Quarterly credit monitoring | Borrower-supplied, sampled data; not service-quality evidence |
| KRO-2026-041 | KRO | Corporate register extract | Filed identity and ownership, not operational control |
| KRO-2026-052 | KRO | Historic trade name and officer filing | Records filed events, not contract supervision |
| DBR-2026-119 | DBR | Annual filing acknowledgement | Receipt only |
| DBR-2026-204 | DBR | Provisional assessment and payment receipt | No substantive review shown |
| NZT-2026-08 | NZT | Outsourced administration thematic note | Sector-level guidance, not a finding against a named company |
| NZT-2026-19 | NZT | Review method and sample | Purposive, non-representative sample |
| NZT-2026-27 | NZT | Follow-up questionnaire summary | Self-reported aggregate responses |
| ZORGLIJN-2026-34 | De Zorglijn | Shared back-office investigation | Supplier-code overlap is suggestive, not conclusive |
| ZORGLIJN-2026-41 | De Zorglijn | Network percentage methodology | Definitions differ; original directories still matter |
| ZORGLIJN-2026-58 | De Zorglijn | Bank concentration notice analysis | Customer identity is not established |
| ZORGLIJN-2026-63 | De Zorglijn | Administrative record explainer | Secondary explainer; consult original records |
| CIVIC-2026-22 | Civic Lens | Address field note | Different address types and dates |
| CIVIC-2026-29 | Civic Lens | Unresolved internal phrases | Original correspondence bundle not reproduced |
| ATLAS-2026-88 | Atlas Registry | Entity alias crosswalk | No additional beneficial-ownership proof |
| WAO-2026-17 | Waypoint Audit Office | Directory sampling protocol | Purposive sample; no guarantee of appointment availability |

The complete machine-readable register is `Sources_Register.csv`.

## Research rules

- A registry can establish what it records, not the quality of an organisation's operations.
- A filing receipt proves receipt or allocation, not the truth of every filed statement.
- A bank record can establish a disclosed financing fact without identifying every customer or proving service outcomes.
- A sector-level oversight note must not be converted into a finding against a named organisation.
- Journalism and field notes can identify leads, but the underlying primary record should be checked.
- Weird or ambiguous language remains unresolved unless the evidence establishes a definition.
- Do not infer an insurer, supplier, owner or decision-maker from a similar name alone.

  A field-note appendix collecting phrases found in fictional administrative correspondence.

  Publisher: Civic Lens

  Scope warning: This document is invented for Coverage Labs. It is not a real bank, government, regulator, court,

  1. “Administratieve terugkeerwind”
  The phrase appears once in an undated draft note attached to a supplier correspondence bundle. No author,
  approved definition or process owner is identified. A later margin comment says: “when the folder comes back but
  nobody remembers who sent it”. Civic Lens cannot establish whether this was an internal joke, a local shorthand or a
  corrupted transcription.

  Research limitation: The phrase is not an established legal, financial or operational term in this fictional source
  environment.

  A meeting note uses “dossierwarmte” to describe the perceived urgency of a case after three hand-offs. The note

  Research limitation: Do not turn colourful internal language into a formal metric.

  Civic Lens retains both phrases because they appear in the documentary trail. The field note labels them unresolved
  language and does not assign a definitive meaning. Readers should preserve the quotation and its uncertainty.

entries.body:
PUBLIC RECORD SIMULATION


  NZT-2026-19

   Thematic review: method and sampling note
  Fictional sector note on outsourced member administration and service continuity.

  Publisher: Nederlands Zorgtoezichtbureau
  Publication date: 2026-09-22
  Record status: Fictional training document

  Scope warning: This document is invented for Coverage Labs. It is not a real bank, government, regulator, court,
  insurer or newsroom record.


  1. Review question
  The NZT reviewed how fictional health-sector organisations map responsibility when intake, document indexing,
  correspondence and case preparation are outsourced. The review was thematic and did not determine whether any
  named insurer breached a legal duty.

  Research limitation: The note is not an enforcement decision and does not establish misconduct by a named
  organisation.




FICTIONAL SOURCE SIMULATION · NO LEGAL OR FINANCIAL EFFECT                                                           01
   2. Sample design
  The review included 12 fictional organisations selected for variation in size and outsourcing model. Six supplied full
  service maps; four supplied partial maps; two supplied no map before the cut-off. The sample is purposive, not
  statistically representative.

   Submission                      Count                                 Treatment

   Full service map                6                                     Reviewed

   Partial service map             4                                     Limitations noted

   No map by cut-off               2                                     Follow-up requested


  Research limitation: The sample cannot be used to estimate prevalence across the entire fictional insurance sector.




FICTIONAL SOURCE SIMULATION · NO LEGAL OR FINANCIAL EFFECT                                                                 02
   3. Findings and recommendations
  Common weaknesses included inconsistent supplier naming, missing exit-plan test dates and unclear escalation
  ownership. The NZT recommends entity-level service maps and member-level incident reporting. Recommendations
  are not findings that every organisation has these weaknesses.

  Research limitation: Do not generalise a thematic observation to an individual company without company-specific
  evidence.




FICTIONAL SOURCE SIMULATION · NO LEGAL OR FINANCIAL EFFECT                                                          03

  The newsroom reviewed fictional case files where a receipt was described as “approval”. In each instance the source

entries.title: BRAND_GUIDE.md
entries.body:
# Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg - Brand and Experience Guide

> All marks, content and names are original fictional training assets.

## Brand concept

Windows 8 Metro / family archive / warm cooperative tiles

## Verbal identity

- Tagline: **Samen vinden we de weg.**
- Secondary line: **Care is a shared journey.**
- Personality: Warm, grounded, practical, generous, family-minded and cooperative.
- Never imply that the visual design proves the product is better.

## Visual system

- Primary: `#b84d35`
- Secondary: `#d87950`
- Accent: `#e4a56d`
- Surface: `#f1d7b7`
- Ink: `#402820`

## Website expression

Flat Metro tiles, warm terracotta and red-brown palette, large typographic labels, household journeys, simple CSS transitions and no glossy card overload.

## Accessibility and motion

All navigation remains keyboard-focusable. Motion is decorative only; Rivierzorg respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. Core information is in HTML, not embedded in images. The fictional status notice remains visible.

## Research presentation

Each company uses its brand vocabulary but the research layer retains common evidence semantics: source IDs, claim IDs, status, confidence, dates, limitations and unknowns.


## Independent operating model — 2026

Kompas is a member-owned cooperative insurer. Its procurement committee rejected the GoedGeregeld enterprise suite in 2021 and retained an independently governed, open-standard case-management stack. The decision is recorded in procurement minutes and a technical architecture note. This does not make Kompas infallible: member governance can be slow, regional capacity remains uneven, and its annual report acknowledges unresolved specialist wait-time gaps. Its distinguishing feature is traceable accountability, not perfection.

# Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg - Evidence Desk

> The registers are the structured research layer. The original source PDFs remain the evidence objects. Status and confidence are distinct fields.

## Claim register quick view

| Claim ID | Topic | Evidence status | Confidence | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLM-01 | Legal identity | Supported | High | Annual report and registry identity records establish the fictional legal names. |
| CLM-02 | Policy terms | Supported | High | Policy guide describes the basis; actual claim-level outcomes are not modelled. |
| CLM-03 | Hospital network | Supported | High | Network annex defines the denominator; capacity and waiting time remain unknown. |
| CLM-04 | Customer service | Disputed | High | The source definitions, numerators and denominators differ materially. |
| CLM-05 | Outsourcing | Partly supported | Medium | Company schedule/technical or board appendix plus supplier register; complete data-processing terms are not public. |
| CLM-06 | Practical access | Unknown | High | No source provides a complete patient-level waiting-time distribution. |
| CLM-07 | Family service | Disputed | High | Family handbook limits named navigation to policyholder, registered partner and dependent children aged 0-17. |
| CLM-08 | Cooperative voting | Disputed | High | Assembly minutes give separate counts for insured persons and eligible cooperative members. |

## Evidence status vocabulary

- **Supported:** the cited fictional source directly supports the bounded claim.
- **Partly supported:** the source supports only part of the claim, or a key document is missing.
- **Disputed:** available sources conflict with the wording or interpretation.
- **Unknown:** the source pack cannot establish the claim.
- **Outdated:** a newer source supersedes the evidence.

## Confidence vocabulary

Confidence describes how confidently the research team has interpreted the available evidence. It is not the same as the evidence status. A disputed conclusion may have High confidence if the source clearly disproves the broad claim.

## Source traceability rule

Use the `source_id` as the stable identifier. Record a page or section in the claim's supporting-source list. Preserve limitations and publication / verification dates. A source being official within the fiction does not make its claims independently verified.

## Registers

- `Claims_Register.csv` - atomic claims and assessments.
- `Sources_Register.csv` - source identity, dates, type, local file and limitations.
- `Open_Questions.md` - unresolved research tasks.

entries.title: Kompas procurement decision — 2021
entries.body: Kompas procurement decision — 2021 FICTIONAL BOARD RECORD / KPX-2021-014 Procurement committee decision: case-management platform Decision date: 18 June 2021. The committee declined the proposed GoedGeregeld enterprise deployment and authorised a cooperative-owned, open-standard case-management environment. Reasons recorded: data portability, transparent configuration, member oversight of access permissions, and the ability to publish service definitions. The minutes also note higher internal maintenance costs and a shortage of specialist technical staff. The decision is evidence of a procurement choice. It does not prove that every Kompas process is transparent or that the alternative system has no suppliers or risks. Kompas wiki

entries.title: Parent_Research.md
entries.body:
# Kompas Gezondheid Groep U.A. - Parent Group Research Dossier

> **FICTIONAL SIMULATION.** This is a completed training example, not a real corporate record, not legal advice and not a statement about any real insurer. All organisations, amounts, people, dates, registers and sources in the simulation are invented.

**Dossier status:** Completed example / evidence-led / provisional assessment only  
**Research snapshot:** 17 November 2026  
**Group:** `Kompas Gezondheid Groep U.A.`  
**Operating insurer:** `Kompas Zorgverzekeraar U.A.`  
**Public brand:** `Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg`  
**Registered office (scenario):** Amersfoort  
**Founded (scenario):** 1978

## 1. Executive identity

A regional cooperative built around family support, member participation and care navigation. Its warm brand hides a precise eligibility system: who counts as family, who is a member, and where the regional promise applies are separate questions. The group reports 250,000 insured persons and a scenario market share of 3.2% (scenario estimate). Its basic policy premium is €168.90 per month. These are fictional company figures and must not be treated as real Dutch market data. [SRC01]

## 2. Legal and corporate identity

| Layer | Entity | Current finding |
|---|---|---|
| Parent group | Kompas Gezondheid Groep U.A. | Group-level strategy, financing and governance |
| Operating insurer | Kompas Zorgverzekeraar U.A. | Legal entity named in the basic policy guide |
| Public-facing brand | Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg | Customer-facing name; not itself proof of legal identity |
| Registered office | Amersfoort | Scenario record; verify against registry extract |
| Shared administration | Kade Data & Dossier B.V. relationship appears in supporting records | Service relationship is not evidence of ownership |

The fictional KRO registry extract distinguishes the parent, insurer and service supplier. A service contract does not, by itself, establish a subsidiary relationship, beneficial ownership or shared decision-making. [SRC08, SRC09, SRC10]

## 3. Corporate history

| Year | Event |
|---|---|
| 1978 | Local member societies in Utrecht and Gelderland establish a cooperative health fund. |
| 1994 | The cooperative adds family assistance desks and a travelling care-navigation service. |
| 2008 | A national basic policy is introduced while local member assemblies retain advisory powers. |
| 2016 | The group creates a formal care-navigation subsidiary and a regional partner directory. |
| 2023 | A family-support pilot expands to include a named navigator for eligible households. |
| 2025 | Members debate the distinction between insured household lives and voting cooperative members. |
| 2027 | Kompas reports the broadest hospital network in this scenario, concentrated in its three core provinces. |


History is reconstructed from the fictional annual report, meeting records and website captures. It is a timeline of published claims, not a verified account of real-world events. [SRC01, SRC05, SRC06]

## 4. Ownership, control and group structure

The annual report describes the group as a member-owned cooperative. That label needs to be separated from the voting and procurement rules. The assembly record shows that insured persons and cooperative members are different populations. [SRC01, SRC06]

**Research finding:** legal ownership, governance participation, operational control and service-provider relationships are four separate questions. Do not treat the corporate group chart as complete until filed ownership, board appointments and contracts are checked.

## 5. Business model and financial profile

- Fictional insured population: 250,000 [SRC01]
- Scenario market share: 3.2% (scenario estimate) [SRC01]
- Basic premium: €168.90 monthly / €2,026.80 annually [SRC02]
- Business model: A regional cooperative built around family support, member participation and care navigation. Its warm brand hides a precise eligibility system: who counts as family, who is a member, and where the regional promise applies are separate questions.
- Financial reporting: the annual report provides group-level premium and expense lines but the public pack does not include a full independent audit opinion or a claim-level profitability reconciliation. [SRC01]

**Do not infer:** premium level alone does not show solvency, efficiency, claims adequacy, care quality or corporate responsibility.

## 6. Outsourcing and third-party dependencies

The document set contains a reference to Kade Data & Dossier B.V. in the service chain. Noordlicht's schedule identifies document intake and first-line file preparation; Rivierzorg's technical architecture shows a Kade Relay exception route; Kompas's board appendix contains supplier code `KDD-04` while redacting the supplier name. [SRC10]

**Evidence status:** Partly supported. The records indicate an administrative service relationship, but the full signed contract, processing agreement, subcontractor register, data-location schedule and tested exit plan are not in the public pack. No conclusion about misconduct or unlawful processing is supported.

## 7. Governance and accountability

| Topic | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Executive responsibility | Board remains responsible for insurer and policy decisions | Supported by scenario annual report |
| Member / shareholder influence | Participation depends on formal legal status and voting rules | Partly supported |
| Procurement oversight | Public records show board-level control, not direct insured-member approval | Supported in available minutes |
| Independent audit | A complete independent audit pack is not included | Unknown |
| Remuneration and conflicts | Summary disclosure only | Partly supported |

## 8. Corporate responsibility

The company's public values page refers to affordability, responsible purchasing and access. The available fictional source pack does not independently test investment exclusions, financed emissions, lobbying, labour standards, executive pay ratios or supplier working conditions. Those topics remain **Unknown**, not negative findings. [SRC01, SRC05]

## 9. Public reputation and complaints

Published complaint/service figures are not comparable across the three insurers. The 95% figure counts hospital organisations with any active agreement. It does not say every hospital site, specialty or treatment route is available. The complaints rate counts upheld formal complaints at year-end and uses a different denominator from the other two companies. [SRC04, SRC08, SRC09]

**Finding:** the headline rates should be reported with their definitions, populations and exclusions. A ranking based on `3.8`, `5.6` and `3.1` alone would be unsound.

## 10. Parent-group assessment summary

| Dimension | Finding | Evidence status | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legal identity | Parent and insurer entities are named in the fictional records | Supported | High |
| Ownership and control | More detail needed on effective control and service-provider influence | Partly supported | Medium |
| Financial transparency | Aggregate figures present; complete independent pack absent | Partly supported | Medium |
| Outsourcing | Administrative relationship indicated; full agreement absent | Partly supported | Medium |
| Governance influence | Formal structures described; practical member influence differs | Partly supported | Medium |
| Corporate responsibility | Marketing commitments exist; implementation evidence is missing | Unknown | Unknown |

No composite score is assigned. The assessment is a source-led summary, not a recommendation.

## 11. Unresolved questions

1. Obtain the full signed service contract and processing annex for Kade Data & Dossier B.V.
2. Identify all subcontractors, data locations, incident responsibilities and exit arrangements.
3. Obtain the complete audited financial statements and notes on related-party transactions.
4. Compare voting eligibility with the number of insured persons and household members.
5. Obtain independent complaints data using a common definition.
6. Verify whether published care-access claims match provider-level contracts and appointment capacity.

## 12. Source index

See `Sources_Register.csv` for source metadata and exact local PDF paths. Key supporting records: SRC01 annual report; SRC06 governance record; SRC08 service/metric record; SRC09 simulated KRO register extract; SRC10 service/outsourcing schedule.

# Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg - Policy Dossier / Insurance Year 2027

> **FICTIONAL SIMULATION ONLY.** All prices, packages and terms below are invented for research practice. They are not real policy terms, real Dutch statutory benefits, or a substitute for an insurer's official contract.

**Provider:** Kompas Zorgverzekeraar U.A.  
**Parent group:** Kompas Gezondheid Groep U.A.  
**Policy year:** 2027  
**Verification date:** 17 November 2026  
**Primary source:** `KOMPAS-SRC-002`

## Product catalogue

### Kompas Ruime Keuze

**Basic insurance | €168.90 / month**

- Ruime naturapolis; annual basic premium €2,026.80.
- Non-contracted care: 85% of the insurer-defined average contracted tariff, subject to policy terms and statutory limits.
- Voluntary deductible options in this exercise: up to €885 on top of the assumed €385 scenario deductible.
- The 95% hospital figure counts hospital organisations with any active contract; the source does not establish the same level of access in every province or specialty.

Source: KOMPAS-SRC-002 and KOMPAS-SRC-008.

### Kompas Basis + Familie

**Supplementary | €23.75 / month**

- 8 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Household support line for the policyholder, registered partner and dependent children aged 0–17.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €350 per policy year.
- The household support line is a service, not an additional insured entitlement for every person in the household.

Source: KOMPAS-SRC-002 and KOMPAS-SRC-007.

### Kompas Plus

**Supplementary | €36.40 / month**

- 12 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 80% up to €500 per policy year; planned treatment may be subject to review.
- Named case-navigation for eligible complex-care cases; local partner capacity varies by province.
- Family navigation does not automatically include adult children living at home or non-registered relatives.

Source: KOMPAS-SRC-002 and KOMPAS-SRC-007.


## Calculation notes

- Monthly premium multiplied by twelve gives the annual basic premium only; add-on costs are separate.
- The assumed €385 deductible is a scenario parameter and should not be carried over into real-world advice.
- Non-contracted reimbursement percentages use a fictional insurer-defined tariff basis. They do not mean the same percentage of an invoice is paid.
- Annual caps are per policy year unless the wording says otherwise.
- Supplementary benefits do not alter the basic-policy contract or create unlimited provider choice.

## Exclusions and conditions to investigate

1. Provider contract and legal entity at the exact treatment location.
2. Whether an annual maximum is per insured person, household, treatment type or policy.
3. Prior authorisation and referral conditions.
4. Waiting periods and exclusions for planned or pre-existing treatment.
5. Treatment definitions, clinical criteria and approved codes.
6. Non-contracted care caps, maximum tariffs and administrative fees.
7. Whether unused sessions roll over and whether multiple packages can be combined.

## Research status

This is a finished training dossier for the supplied source pack. It is not a complete real-world policy audit. Unknown items remain unknown; do not infer them from marketing copy or from the package name.

# Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg - Insurance Provider Research Dossier

> **FICTIONAL SIMULATION.** This completed training example does not describe a real insurance provider, contract or Dutch healthcare entitlement.

**Dossier status:** Completed example / policy and provider-access focus  
**Verification date:** 17 November 2026  
**Public brand:** Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg  
**Legal insurer:** Kompas Zorgverzekeraar U.A.  
**Parent group:** Kompas Gezondheid Groep U.A.  
**Basic policy:** Kompas Ruime Keuze  
**Product type:** Ruime naturapolis

## 1. Identity and legal responsibility

The brand is the customer-facing identity. The fictional policy guide names `Kompas Zorgverzekeraar U.A.` as the insurer, and the annual report identifies `Kompas Gezondheid Groep U.A.` as the parent group. These are separate legal and commercial layers. [SRC01, SRC02]

## 2. Basic policy and price

| Field | Scenario value |
|---|---|
| Policy | Kompas Ruime Keuze |
| Type | Ruime naturapolis |
| Monthly premium | €168.90 |
| Annual premium | €2,026.80 |
| Non-contracted care | 85% of the insurer-defined average contracted tariff, subject to policy terms and statutory limits |
| Assumed deductible | €385 scenario parameter; voluntary options up to €885 |
| Hospital network headline | 95% |

The deductible is a fictional scenario parameter. It is not intended as a statement of the actual statutory deductible for any real policy year. Reimbursement is based on the insurer-defined tariff and may be affected by a cap, exclusion, authorisation requirement, provider type or treatment code. [SRC02]

## 3. Supplementary packages

### Kompas Basis + Familie

**Supplementary - €23.75 / month**

- 8 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Household support line for the policyholder, registered partner and dependent children aged 0–17.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €350 per policy year.
- The household support line is a service, not an additional insured entitlement for every person in the household.

Source: KOMPAS-SRC-002 and KOMPAS-SRC-007.

### Kompas Plus

**Supplementary - €36.40 / month**

- 12 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 80% up to €500 per policy year; planned treatment may be subject to review.
- Named case-navigation for eligible complex-care cases; local partner capacity varies by province.
- Family navigation does not automatically include adult children living at home or non-registered relatives.

Source: KOMPAS-SRC-002 and KOMPAS-SRC-007.


## 4. Provider choice and network access

Headline network figure: **95%**. The 95% figure counts hospital organisations with any active agreement. It does not say every hospital site, specialty or treatment route is available. The complaints rate counts upheld formal complaints at year-end and uses a different denominator from the other two companies. [SRC03, SRC07/SRC08]

The percentage must be read as an administrative directory indicator. It does not establish availability for a specific provider, site, specialty, date or patient pathway. A complete access check would need the exact legal entity, location, service code, contract period, referral pathway, capacity and waiting time.

## 5. Care-specific evidence

| Care area | Published description | Evidence limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Mental healthcare | Dedicated navigation and wait-list mediation are available; actual treatment waits still depend on contracted providers and local capacity. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Gender-affirming healthcare | Partner-centre referrals and a named navigator are available; prior approval applies to specified procedures. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Women's healthcare | Broad midwifery and hospital network in Utrecht, Gelderland and Flevoland; pelvic-health partners are less dense outside the core area. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Disability and rehabilitation | Named case manager for eligible complex cases; strong assistive-device and rehabilitation coordination in the core provinces. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Physiotherapy and dental | Plus includes 12 sessions and 80% dental up to €500; exclusions can apply to pre-existing treatment plans. | Company report / not an access guarantee |

## 6. Customer service and complaints

The published complaint/service figure is **3.1 / 1,000**. The 95% figure counts hospital organisations with any active agreement. It does not say every hospital site, specialty or treatment route is available. The complaints rate counts upheld formal complaints at year-end and uses a different denominator from the other two companies. [SRC04, SRC09]

The complaint measure is not directly comparable with the other companies. The numerator and denominator differ: upheld formal complaints divided by year-end insured count. Report this metric with that definition, or omit it from a cross-company ranking.

## 7. Practical-access checklist

For a real or simulated treatment scenario, record:

1. Exact treatment and service code.
2. Named provider and contracting legal entity.
3. Treatment location and policy-year contract status.
4. Referral, clinical indication and prior-authorisation conditions.
5. Reimbursement basis, maximum tariff, annual cap and likely patient share.
6. Current waiting-time information and continuity arrangements.
7. Travel, accessibility, language and support needs.

## 8. Claim-level assessment

| Claim | Status | Confidence | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brand / legal insurer relationship | Supported | High | Named in policy guide and annual report |
| Published premium and benefit summary | Supported | High | Stated in fictional policy guide; full terms still matter |
| Practical availability of all advertised pathways | Unknown | Medium | No patient-level capacity and waiting-time dataset |
| Network headline as a measure of access | Disputed | High | Source denominator does not measure specialty or appointments |
| Cross-company complaint ranking | Disputed | High | Definitions and denominators differ |

## 9. Strengths, constraints and unresolved matters

**Potential strengths**
- Care navigation and stronger support in core provinces.

**Potential constraints**
- Highest premium, regional unevenness and eligibility limits in family navigation.

**Still unknown**
- Individual provider contracts and actual appointment capacity.
- Complete policy wording and claim-level examples.
- Independent customer-outcome evidence.
- Full data-processing and subcontractor arrangements.

## 10. Conclusion

Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg presents a distinct policy and service proposition in this fictional scenario. A suitability conclusion depends on a person's location, provider, treatment needs, policy combination and risk tolerance. No overall recommendation or score is assigned.

## Sources

See `Sources_Register.csv`. Start with SRC02 (policy), SRC03 (network), SRC04 (service), and company-specific SRC06-SRC10 records. All sources are fictional training artefacts.

  A simple reading guide                                                                    L Y
 Reading lens                      What to record                                        ON

entries.title: Wiki.md
entries.body:
# Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg - Fictional Company Wiki

> **FICTIONAL SIMULATION.** This is a secondary training article. The organisation, people, policies, prices, documents, events and figures are invented. It is not a real company, insurer, policy or legal record.

## Overview

A regional cooperative built around family support, member participation and care navigation. Its warm brand hides a precise eligibility system: who counts as family, who is a member, and where the regional promise applies are separate questions.

## Corporate profile

- **Parent group:** Kompas Gezondheid Groep U.A.
- **Legal insurer:** Kompas Zorgverzekeraar U.A.
- **Public brand:** Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg
- **Registered office (scenario):** Amersfoort
- **Founded (scenario):** 1978
- **Insured population:** 250,000
- **Scenario market share:** 3.2% (scenario estimate)
- **Company model:** Regional member cooperative

## History

- **1978:** Local member societies in Utrecht and Gelderland establish a cooperative health fund.
- **1994:** The cooperative adds family assistance desks and a travelling care-navigation service.
- **2008:** A national basic policy is introduced while local member assemblies retain advisory powers.
- **2016:** The group creates a formal care-navigation subsidiary and a regional partner directory.
- **2023:** A family-support pilot expands to include a named navigator for eligible households.
- **2025:** Members debate the distinction between insured household lives and voting cooperative members.
- **2027:** Kompas reports the broadest hospital network in this scenario, concentrated in its three core provinces.

## Insurance products

### Kompas Ruime Keuze

**Basic insurance - €168.90 / month**
- Ruime naturapolis; annual basic premium €2,026.80.
- Non-contracted care: 85% of the insurer-defined average contracted tariff, subject to policy terms and statutory limits.
- Voluntary deductible options in this exercise: up to €885 on top of the assumed €385 scenario deductible.
- The 95% hospital figure counts hospital organisations with any active contract; the source does not establish the same level of access in every province or specialty.
### Kompas Basis + Familie

**Supplementary - €23.75 / month**
- 8 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Household support line for the policyholder, registered partner and dependent children aged 0–17.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €350 per policy year.
- The household support line is a service, not an additional insured entitlement for every person in the household.
### Kompas Plus

**Supplementary - €36.40 / month**
- 12 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 80% up to €500 per policy year; planned treatment may be subject to review.
- Named case-navigation for eligible complex-care cases; local partner capacity varies by province.
- Family navigation does not automatically include adult children living at home or non-registered relatives.

## Care access

- **Mental healthcare:** Dedicated navigation and wait-list mediation are available; actual treatment waits still depend on contracted providers and local capacity.
- **Gender-affirming healthcare:** Partner-centre referrals and a named navigator are available; prior approval applies to specified procedures.
- **Women's healthcare:** Broad midwifery and hospital network in Utrecht, Gelderland and Flevoland; pelvic-health partners are less dense outside the core area.
- **Disability and rehabilitation:** Named case manager for eligible complex cases; strong assistive-device and rehabilitation coordination in the core provinces.
- **Physiotherapy and dental:** Plus includes 12 sessions and 80% dental up to €500; exclusions can apply to pre-existing treatment plans.

## Customer service and public metrics

- **Headline premium:** €168.90 monthly.
- **Hospital network headline:** 95%.
- **Published complaints/service rate:** 3.1 / 1,000.

These measures are not directly comparable across the three fictional companies. Their numerators, denominators, periods and exclusions differ. The network figures describe administrative directory measures, not appointment access or clinical capacity.

## Governance, service partners and unresolved questions

The cooperative distinguishes insured persons from registered voting members. Family navigation is narrower than the full household and is limited by age and registration rules.

The source pack contains references to a shared administrative service environment. A service relationship is not proof of ownership, unlawful processing, shared claim decisions or common corporate control. The full contract, processing annex, subcontractor list and operational audit are not available.

## Primary sources

See `Sources_Register.csv` and the `Sources/` folder. The wiki is not a substitute for the policy guide, corporate report, network annex, governance records or supplier schedule.

## Research links

- [Research overview](../research/overview.html)
- [Parent group dossier](../research/Parent_Research.md)
- [Provider dossier](../research/Provider_Research.md)
- [Policy dossier](../research/Policy_Research.md)
- [Evidence desk](../research/Evidence_Desk.md)

## Editorial note

Check every material statement against the linked fictional primary source. Preserve evidence status, confidence and source limitations separately. All material is fictional training content.

entries.title: METHOD.md
entries.body:
# Research Method - Completed Training Dossiers

> **All source organisations, records, people, figures, policy terms and events in this lab are fictional.** This is a closed practice environment. It does not represent the Dutch state, a real regulator, a real insurer or real health coverage.

## A repeatable evidence method

1. Resolve the entity: parent group, operating insurer, brand, policy and service suppliers are different records.
2. Atomise the claim: one proposition per claim record.
3. Record source identity, publisher, URL or local path, publication date, verification date, page/section, source type and limitations.
4. Distinguish company assertion, primary record, independent reporting, regulatory-style record, provider-side evidence and user testimony.
5. Set evidence status and confidence separately.
6. Trace both support and contradiction. Never hide conflicts by choosing the tidier source.
7. Keep legal entitlement, contractual entitlement and practical accessibility separate.
8. For care access, require a named provider, site, treatment, service code, referral, contract period, capacity and wait-time evidence.
9. For customer metrics, record numerator, denominator, population, exclusions, period and channel.
10. Preserve unknowns. Do not calculate an overall winner from incomparable or incomplete evidence.

## Company experiences are intentionally different

- **Noordlicht:** desktop archaeology. Explore visual brand layers, member governance records, supplier schedules and archive snapshots.
- **Rivierzorg:** systems investigation. Follow event codes, API fields, queues, service-level definitions and network data.
- **Kompas:** household and cooperative research. Separate insured lives, household eligibility, member status, voting rights and regional service boundaries.

The research method overlaps, but the discovery interface and evidence types vary. This models the fact that a good researcher adapts source-finding tactics to an organisation rather than repeating one identical checklist.

## Fictional institutions and external sources

The KRO, DBR, NZT, Noorder Cooperative Bank and De Zorglijn are invented institutions and publications. They are labelled as simulations throughout the files. Their names intentionally evoke the functions of public registers, tax filing services, financial oversight, banks and specialist journalism without impersonating real institutions.

## Hidden cross-company case

The learner-facing hypothesis ledger is part of the Academy. It carries the former cross-company case method: competing explanations, supporting and contradictory evidence, source gaps, falsifiers and bounded conclusions. Facilitator-only archived materials remain outside the served application.


## Expanded cross-company case: unresolved infrastructure hypothesis

The shared case adds three simulated archive exhibits (NLX-2026-01, RVX-2026-02 and KPX-2026-03). They are intentionally incomplete leads, not proof of a conspiracy. Keep ordinary consolidation, quiet common infrastructure, fragmented systems with a common vendor, and changing arrangements as competing explanations. No supplied source proves coordinated intent, a single hidden controller or harm to members. A strong investigation may conclude that selected supplier, capital and workflow relationships exist while the full structure and practical effects remain unknown.

entries.body:
# Noordlicht Zorg - Evidence Desk

> The registers are the structured research layer. The original source PDFs remain the evidence objects. Status and confidence are distinct fields.

## Claim register quick view

| Claim ID | Topic | Evidence status | Confidence | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLM-01 | Legal identity | Supported | High | Annual report and registry identity records establish the fictional legal names. |
| CLM-02 | Policy terms | Supported | High | Policy guide describes the basis; actual claim-level outcomes are not modelled. |
| CLM-03 | Hospital network | Supported | High | Network annex defines the denominator; capacity and waiting time remain unknown. |
| CLM-04 | Customer service | Disputed | High | The source definitions, numerators and denominators differ materially. |
| CLM-05 | Outsourcing | Partly supported | Medium | Company schedule/technical or board appendix plus supplier register; complete data-processing terms are not public. |
| CLM-06 | Practical access | Unknown | High | No source provides a complete patient-level waiting-time distribution. |
| CLM-07 | Member governance | Disputed | High | Assembly minutes distinguish insured persons, delegates and executive procurement authority. |
| CLM-08 | Halo pathway | Disputed | High | The pathway is described across three regions; no national queue is evidenced. |

## Evidence status vocabulary

- **Supported:** the cited fictional source directly supports the bounded claim.
- **Partly supported:** the source supports only part of the claim, or a key document is missing.
- **Disputed:** available sources conflict with the wording or interpretation.
- **Unknown:** the source pack cannot establish the claim.
- **Outdated:** a newer source supersedes the evidence.

## Confidence vocabulary

Confidence describes how confidently the research team has interpreted the available evidence. It is not the same as the evidence status. A disputed conclusion may have High confidence if the source clearly disproves the broad claim.

## Source traceability rule

Use the `source_id` as the stable identifier. Record a page or section in the claim's supporting-source list. Preserve limitations and publication / verification dates. A source being official within the fiction does not make its claims independently verified.

## Registers

- `Claims_Register.csv` - atomic claims and assessments.
- `Sources_Register.csv` - source identity, dates, type, local file and limitations.
- `Open_Questions.md` - unresolved research tasks.
