entries.title: Parent_Research.md
entries.body:
# Noordlicht Holding U.A. - Parent Group Research Dossier

> **FICTIONAL SIMULATION.** This is a completed training example, not a real corporate record, not legal advice and not a statement about any real insurer. All organisations, amounts, people, dates, registers and sources in the simulation are invented.

**Dossier status:** Completed example / evidence-led / provisional assessment only  
**Research snapshot:** 17 November 2026  
**Group:** `Noordlicht Holding U.A.`  
**Operating insurer:** `Noordlicht Zorgverzekeraar N.V.`  
**Public brand:** `Noordlicht Zorg`  
**Registered office (scenario):** Zwolle  
**Founded (scenario):** 2001

## 1. Executive identity

A member-led insurer with a glossy future-facing public image and a dense regional history beneath it. Noordlicht grew from mutual-aid funds into a national group, but its most dependable relationships are still regional. The group reports 510,000 insured persons and a scenario market share of 6.4% (scenario estimate). Its basic policy premium is €159.75 per month. These are fictional company figures and must not be treated as real Dutch market data. [SRC01]

## 2. Legal and corporate identity

| Layer | Entity | Current finding |
|---|---|---|
| Parent group | Noordlicht Holding U.A. | Group-level strategy, financing and governance |
| Operating insurer | Noordlicht Zorgverzekeraar N.V. | Legal entity named in the basic policy guide |
| Public-facing brand | Noordlicht Zorg | Customer-facing name; not itself proof of legal identity |
| Registered office | Zwolle | Scenario record; verify against registry extract |
| Shared administration | Kade Data & Dossier B.V. relationship appears in supporting records | Service relationship is not evidence of ownership |

The fictional KRO registry extract distinguishes the parent, insurer and service supplier. A service contract does not, by itself, establish a subsidiary relationship, beneficial ownership or shared decision-making. [SRC08, SRC09, SRC10]

## 3. Corporate history

| Year | Event |
|---|---|
| 2001 | Three Overijssel and Gelderland mutual-aid funds combine under the Noordlicht name. |
| 2007 | The group launches its first national basic policy while retaining a member council. |
| 2014 | Noordlicht buys a small digital claims platform and brings first-line administration in-house. |
| 2021 | The group starts the Halo pathway for complex and gender-affirming care in three university-hospital regions. |
| 2025 | A multi-year case-administration agreement is extended; the public annual report describes it as a continuity partnership. |
| 2027 | The company markets a national network while its detailed directory still shows regional differences by treatment and site. |


History is reconstructed from the fictional annual report, meeting records and website captures. It is a timeline of published claims, not a verified account of real-world events. [SRC01, SRC05, SRC06]

## 4. Ownership, control and group structure

The annual report describes the group as a member-owned cooperative. That label needs to be separated from the voting and procurement rules. The member assembly record shows a delegate-based model and leaves supplier procurement with the executive board. [SRC01, SRC06]

**Research finding:** legal ownership, governance participation, operational control and service-provider relationships are four separate questions. Do not treat the corporate group chart as complete until filed ownership, board appointments and contracts are checked.

## 5. Business model and financial profile

- Fictional insured population: 510,000 [SRC01]
- Scenario market share: 6.4% (scenario estimate) [SRC01]
- Basic premium: €159.75 monthly / €1,917.00 annually [SRC02]
- Business model: A member-led insurer with a glossy future-facing public image and a dense regional history beneath it. Noordlicht grew from mutual-aid funds into a national group, but its most dependable relationships are still regional.
- Financial reporting: the annual report provides group-level premium and expense lines but the public pack does not include a full independent audit opinion or a claim-level profitability reconciliation. [SRC01]

**Do not infer:** premium level alone does not show solvency, efficiency, claims adequacy, care quality or corporate responsibility.

## 6. Outsourcing and third-party dependencies

The document set contains a reference to Kade Data & Dossier B.V. in the service chain. Noordlicht's schedule identifies document intake and first-line file preparation; Rivierzorg's technical architecture shows a Kade Relay exception route; Kompas's board appendix contains supplier code `KDD-04` while redacting the supplier name. [SRC10]

**Evidence status:** Partly supported. The records indicate an administrative service relationship, but the full signed contract, processing agreement, subcontractor register, data-location schedule and tested exit plan are not in the public pack. No conclusion about misconduct or unlawful processing is supported.

## 7. Governance and accountability

| Topic | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Executive responsibility | Board remains responsible for insurer and policy decisions | Supported by scenario annual report |
| Member / shareholder influence | Participation depends on formal legal status and voting rules | Partly supported |
| Procurement oversight | Public records show board-level control, not direct insured-member approval | Supported in available minutes |
| Independent audit | A complete independent audit pack is not included | Unknown |
| Remuneration and conflicts | Summary disclosure only | Partly supported |

## 8. Corporate responsibility

The company's public values page refers to affordability, responsible purchasing and access. The available fictional source pack does not independently test investment exclusions, financed emissions, lobbying, labour standards, executive pay ratios or supplier working conditions. Those topics remain **Unknown**, not negative findings. [SRC01, SRC05]

## 9. Public reputation and complaints

Published complaint/service figures are not comparable across the three insurers. The 92% figure is based on hospital organisations in the public directory, not the number of sites or every specialty. The complaints rate excludes contacts resolved before a formal complaint is registered. [SRC04, SRC08, SRC09]

**Finding:** the headline rates should be reported with their definitions, populations and exclusions. A ranking based on `3.8`, `5.6` and `3.1` alone would be unsound.

## 10. Parent-group assessment summary

| Dimension | Finding | Evidence status | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legal identity | Parent and insurer entities are named in the fictional records | Supported | High |
| Ownership and control | More detail needed on effective control and service-provider influence | Partly supported | Medium |
| Financial transparency | Aggregate figures present; complete independent pack absent | Partly supported | Medium |
| Outsourcing | Administrative relationship indicated; full agreement absent | Partly supported | Medium |
| Governance influence | Formal structures described; practical member influence differs | Partly supported | Medium |
| Corporate responsibility | Marketing commitments exist; implementation evidence is missing | Unknown | Unknown |

No composite score is assigned. The assessment is a source-led summary, not a recommendation.

## 11. Unresolved questions

1. Obtain the full signed service contract and processing annex for Kade Data & Dossier B.V.
2. Identify all subcontractors, data locations, incident responsibilities and exit arrangements.
3. Obtain the complete audited financial statements and notes on related-party transactions.
4. Compare voting eligibility with the number of insured persons and household members.
5. Obtain independent complaints data using a common definition.
6. Verify whether published care-access claims match provider-level contracts and appointment capacity.

## 12. Source index

See `Sources_Register.csv` for source metadata and exact local PDF paths. Key supporting records: SRC01 annual report; SRC06 governance record; SRC08 service/metric record; SRC09 simulated KRO register extract; SRC10 service/outsourcing schedule.

# Noordlicht Zorg - Policy Dossier / Insurance Year 2027

> **FICTIONAL SIMULATION ONLY.** All prices, packages and terms below are invented for research practice. They are not real policy terms, real Dutch statutory benefits, or a substitute for an insurer's official contract.

**Provider:** Noordlicht Zorgverzekeraar N.V.  
**Parent group:** Noordlicht Holding U.A.  
**Policy year:** 2027  
**Verification date:** 17 November 2026  
**Primary source:** `NOORDLICHT-SRC-002`

## Product catalogue

### Noordlicht Basis

**Basic insurance | €159.75 / month**

- Naturapolis; annual basic premium €1,917.00.
- Non-contracted care: 70% of the average contracted tariff as defined in the reimbursement schedule; caps and exclusions apply.
- Voluntary deductible options in this exercise: up to €885 on top of the assumed €385 scenario deductible.
- Hospital directory: 92% headline figure; the source counts hospital organisations, not all treatment locations.

Source: NOORDLICHT-SRC-002 and NOORDLICHT-SRC-007.

### Noordlicht Extra

**Supplementary | €20.90 / month**

- 9 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €350 per policy year.
- One optical contribution up to €75 every two calendar years.
- No automatic reimbursement for non-contracted supplementary providers; reimbursement depends on the supplementary schedule.

Source: NOORDLICHT-SRC-002.

### Noordlicht Extra Plus

**Supplementary | €34.50 / month**

- 12 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €500 per policy year, subject to treatment-plan review.
- Optical contribution up to €125 every two calendar years.
- Some planned dental treatment requires prior acceptance; existing treatment plans may be excluded.

Source: NOORDLICHT-SRC-002.


## Calculation notes

- Monthly premium multiplied by twelve gives the annual basic premium only; add-on costs are separate.
- The assumed €385 deductible is a scenario parameter and should not be carried over into real-world advice.
- Non-contracted reimbursement percentages use a fictional insurer-defined tariff basis. They do not mean the same percentage of an invoice is paid.
- Annual caps are per policy year unless the wording says otherwise.
- Supplementary benefits do not alter the basic-policy contract or create unlimited provider choice.

## Exclusions and conditions to investigate

1. Provider contract and legal entity at the exact treatment location.
2. Whether an annual maximum is per insured person, household, treatment type or policy.
3. Prior authorisation and referral conditions.
4. Waiting periods and exclusions for planned or pre-existing treatment.
5. Treatment definitions, clinical criteria and approved codes.
6. Non-contracted care caps, maximum tariffs and administrative fees.
7. Whether unused sessions roll over and whether multiple packages can be combined.

## Research status

This is a finished training dossier for the supplied source pack. It is not a complete real-world policy audit. Unknown items remain unknown; do not infer them from marketing copy or from the package name.

# Noordlicht Zorg - Insurance Provider Research Dossier

> **FICTIONAL SIMULATION.** This completed training example does not describe a real insurance provider, contract or Dutch healthcare entitlement.

**Dossier status:** Completed example / policy and provider-access focus  
**Verification date:** 17 November 2026  
**Public brand:** Noordlicht Zorg  
**Legal insurer:** Noordlicht Zorgverzekeraar N.V.  
**Parent group:** Noordlicht Holding U.A.  
**Basic policy:** Noordlicht Basis  
**Product type:** Naturapolis

## 1. Identity and legal responsibility

The brand is the customer-facing identity. The fictional policy guide names `Noordlicht Zorgverzekeraar N.V.` as the insurer, and the annual report identifies `Noordlicht Holding U.A.` as the parent group. These are separate legal and commercial layers. [SRC01, SRC02]

## 2. Basic policy and price

| Field | Scenario value |
|---|---|
| Policy | Noordlicht Basis |
| Type | Naturapolis |
| Monthly premium | €159.75 |
| Annual premium | €1,917.00 |
| Non-contracted care | 70% of the insurer-defined average contracted tariff; schedule caps may reduce payment |
| Assumed deductible | €385 scenario parameter; voluntary options up to €885 |
| Hospital network headline | 92% |

The deductible is a fictional scenario parameter. It is not intended as a statement of the actual statutory deductible for any real policy year. Reimbursement is based on the insurer-defined tariff and may be affected by a cap, exclusion, authorisation requirement, provider type or treatment code. [SRC02]

## 3. Supplementary packages

### Noordlicht Extra

**Supplementary - €20.90 / month**

- 9 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €350 per policy year.
- One optical contribution up to €75 every two calendar years.
- No automatic reimbursement for non-contracted supplementary providers; reimbursement depends on the supplementary schedule.

Source: NOORDLICHT-SRC-002.

### Noordlicht Extra Plus

**Supplementary - €34.50 / month**

- 12 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €500 per policy year, subject to treatment-plan review.
- Optical contribution up to €125 every two calendar years.
- Some planned dental treatment requires prior acceptance; existing treatment plans may be excluded.

Source: NOORDLICHT-SRC-002.


## 4. Provider choice and network access

Headline network figure: **92%**. The 92% figure is based on hospital organisations in the public directory, not the number of sites or every specialty. The complaints rate excludes contacts resolved before a formal complaint is registered. [SRC03, SRC07/SRC08]

The percentage must be read as an administrative directory indicator. It does not establish availability for a specific provider, site, specialty, date or patient pathway. A complete access check would need the exact legal entity, location, service code, contract period, referral pathway, capacity and waiting time.

## 5. Care-specific evidence

| Care area | Published description | Evidence limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Mental healthcare | Broad national contracted network; triage target is 14 days to first contact. Treatment waits vary by provider and region. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Gender-affirming healthcare | Halo pathway links three university-hospital regions; prior coordination is required for selected treatments. No source establishes one national appointment queue. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Women's healthcare | Contracted midwifery and gynaecology; pelvic-floor physiotherapy depends on indication and provider contract. Endometriosis and menopause pathways vary by region. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Disability and rehabilitation | Medical aids through contracted suppliers; a coordinator may be assigned after referral for eligible complex cases. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Physiotherapy and dental | Extra includes 9 sessions and 75% dental up to €350; the basic-policy and supplementary entitlements are separate. | Company report / not an access guarantee |

## 6. Customer service and complaints

The published complaint/service figure is **3.8 / 1,000**. The 92% figure is based on hospital organisations in the public directory, not the number of sites or every specialty. The complaints rate excludes contacts resolved before a formal complaint is registered. [SRC04, SRC08]

The complaint measure is not directly comparable with the other companies. The numerator and denominator differ: formal complaints only; first-contact and supplier-handled contacts are excluded. Report this metric with that definition, or omit it from a cross-company ranking.

## 7. Practical-access checklist

For a real or simulated treatment scenario, record:

1. Exact treatment and service code.
2. Named provider and contracting legal entity.
3. Treatment location and policy-year contract status.
4. Referral, clinical indication and prior-authorisation conditions.
5. Reimbursement basis, maximum tariff, annual cap and likely patient share.
6. Current waiting-time information and continuity arrangements.
7. Travel, accessibility, language and support needs.

## 8. Claim-level assessment

| Claim | Status | Confidence | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brand / legal insurer relationship | Supported | High | Named in policy guide and annual report |
| Published premium and benefit summary | Supported | High | Stated in fictional policy guide; full terms still matter |
| Practical availability of all advertised pathways | Unknown | Medium | No patient-level capacity and waiting-time dataset |
| Network headline as a measure of access | Disputed | High | Source denominator does not measure specialty or appointments |
| Cross-company complaint ranking | Disputed | High | Definitions and denominators differ |

## 9. Strengths, constraints and unresolved matters

**Potential strengths**
- Coordinated Halo pathway and broad national contracted care.

**Potential constraints**
- Non-contracted reimbursement is limited; the Halo pathway is regionally concentrated.

**Still unknown**
- Individual provider contracts and actual appointment capacity.
- Complete policy wording and claim-level examples.
- Independent customer-outcome evidence.
- Full data-processing and subcontractor arrangements.

## 10. Conclusion

Noordlicht Zorg presents a distinct policy and service proposition in this fictional scenario. A suitability conclusion depends on a person's location, provider, treatment needs, policy combination and risk tolerance. No overall recommendation or score is assigned.

## Sources

## Overview

- **Registered office (scenario):** Zwolle
- **Founded (scenario):** 2001
- **Insured population:** 510,000
- **Scenario market share:** 6.4% (scenario estimate)
- **Company model:** Mutual-style cooperative group

## History

- **2001:** Three Overijssel and Gelderland mutual-aid funds combine under the Noordlicht name.
- **2007:** The group launches its first national basic policy while retaining a member council.
- **2014:** Noordlicht buys a small digital claims platform and brings first-line administration in-house.
- **2021:** The group starts the Halo pathway for complex and gender-affirming care in three university-hospital regions.
- **2025:** A multi-year case-administration agreement is extended; the public annual report describes it as a continuity partnership.
- **2027:** The company markets a national network while its detailed directory still shows regional differences by treatment and site.

## Insurance products

### Noordlicht Basis

**Basic insurance - €159.75 / month**
- Naturapolis; annual basic premium €1,917.00.
- Non-contracted care: 70% of the average contracted tariff as defined in the reimbursement schedule; caps and exclusions apply.
- Voluntary deductible options in this exercise: up to €885 on top of the assumed €385 scenario deductible.
- Hospital directory: 92% headline figure; the source counts hospital organisations, not all treatment locations.
### Noordlicht Extra

**Supplementary - €20.90 / month**
- 9 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €350 per policy year.
- One optical contribution up to €75 every two calendar years.
- No automatic reimbursement for non-contracted supplementary providers; reimbursement depends on the supplementary schedule.
### Noordlicht Extra Plus

**Supplementary - €34.50 / month**
- 12 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €500 per policy year, subject to treatment-plan review.
- Optical contribution up to €125 every two calendar years.
- Some planned dental treatment requires prior acceptance; existing treatment plans may be excluded.

## Care access

- **Mental healthcare:** Broad national contracted network; triage target is 14 days to first contact. Treatment waits vary by provider and region.
- **Gender-affirming healthcare:** Halo pathway links three university-hospital regions; prior coordination is required for selected treatments. No source establishes one national appointment queue.
- **Women's healthcare:** Contracted midwifery and gynaecology; pelvic-floor physiotherapy depends on indication and provider contract. Endometriosis and menopause pathways vary by region.
- **Disability and rehabilitation:** Medical aids through contracted suppliers; a coordinator may be assigned after referral for eligible complex cases.
- **Physiotherapy and dental:** Extra includes 9 sessions and 75% dental up to €350; the basic-policy and supplementary entitlements are separate.

## Customer service and public metrics

- **Headline premium:** €159.75 monthly.
- **Hospital network headline:** 92%.
- **Published complaints/service rate:** 3.8 / 1,000.

These measures are not directly comparable across the three fictional companies. Their numerators, denominators, periods and exclusions differ. The network figures describe administrative directory measures, not appointment access or clinical capacity.

## Governance, service partners and unresolved questions

The company describes itself as member-owned. Its assembly minutes distinguish voting delegates from all insured people and state that supplier procurement remains with the executive board.

The source pack contains references to a shared administrative service environment. A service relationship is not proof of ownership, unlawful processing, shared claim decisions or common corporate control. The full contract, processing annex, subcontractor list and operational audit are not available.

## Primary sources

See `Sources_Register.csv` and the `Sources/` folder. The wiki is not a substitute for the policy guide, corporate report, network annex, governance records or supplier schedule.

## Research links

- [Research overview](../research/overview.html)
- [Parent group dossier](../research/Parent_Research.md)
- [Provider dossier](../research/Provider_Research.md)
- [Policy dossier](../research/Policy_Research.md)
- [Evidence desk](../research/Evidence_Desk.md)

## Editorial note

Check every material statement against the linked fictional primary source. Preserve evidence status, confidence and source limitations separately. All material is fictional training content.

entries.title: README.md
entries.body:
# PALISADE — fictional exam company

Palisade is a fictional training world created for Coverage Labs V0.1.4. Its visual identity draws on late-1970s European airport wayfinding, civic information terminals and printed travel ephemera. The current visual palette is witchy pastel sage green, lavender and purple-goth: deep aubergine, muted violet, soft lilac and pale green. All entities, people, contracts, metrics, records and events are invented.

The exam case is **Every Region, Within Reach?** The learner must independently investigate the public access claim, corporate structure, delegated operations, metric definition, source limitations and unresolved member outcomes.

Learner entry points: `website/index.html`, `wiki/index.html`, `research/desk.html`.


## Current visual palette — V0.1.4.1.1

- Deep aubergine: `#24192D` / night `#17111F`
- Goth purple: `#76518B`
- Soft violet: `#A98BC2`
- Pastel sage: `#B9D5AD`
- Pale mint: `#DCEBD5`
- Ghost lilac: `#E5D9ED`
- Paper: `#F4EFF3`

The same palette is used by the public website, wiki, research desk, independent exam workspace and Coverage Labs world card. The original source records and their evidential content are unchanged.

## Background systems note

**Background workflow platform (fictional):** Palisade uses a separate GoedGeregeld GG Route Board tenant for regional directory-review tasks and bulletin workflow. The software tracks review tasks; it does not create provider capacity or guarantee a route to an appointment.

PALISADE / CIVIC ROUTE DOSSIER




 PALISADE / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD


           Palisade Civic Health Group — Annual
                        Review 2025
 PAL-SRC-001 • Parent company • Issued 2026-02-18

 Purpose in this simulation: Establishes group structure, stated strategy, consolidated activity and limits of
 parent-level reporting.


 DOCUMENT CONTROL
 This document is invented for Coverage Labs. It does not describe a real insurer, regulator, provider, person or event. Its
 contents are evidence only within the fictional Palisade investigation.



 01 / Purpose and perimeter
 Palisade Civic Health Group N.V. describes itself as the coordinating parent of a group that designs, funds and
 administers regional health-cover services. The review consolidates the parent and two wholly controlled subsidiaries. It
 does not consolidate independent contracted care providers.

 02 / Group structure
 The parent owns Palisade Zorgverzekering N.V. (the risk-bearing insurance provider) and Palisade Route Services B.V.
 (a service company responsible for directory maintenance, appointment routing and member contact operations).
 Regional care providers remain independent counterparties.




FICTIONAL SIMULATION MATERIAL                                                                            PAL-SRC-001 • PAGE 1
 PALISADE / CIVIC ROUTE DOSSIER




 03 / Access promise
 The group strategy uses the phrase “care within reach in every region”. The annual review defines reach as the presence
 of at least one contracted route for each listed care category in each service region. It does not define reach as a
 guaranteed appointment, travel-time ceiling or acceptance by a particular clinician.

 04 / Performance summary
 The parent reports that 94% of region/category combinations had at least one route listed at year end. The measure is
 based on a directory snapshot. The report does not state whether routes were accepting new referrals on the snapshot
 date.




FICTIONAL SIMULATION MATERIAL                                                                        PAL-SRC-001 • PAGE 2
 PALISADE / CIVIC ROUTE DOSSIER




 05 / Risk and limitation
 Management identifies directory freshness, provider capacity and referral hand-offs as operational risks. The report says
 Route Services receives monthly availability files from providers, but does not provide the underlying files or a
 reconciliation rate.

 06 / Governance
 The parent board sets group strategy and approves the annual service framework. The insurance provider retains
 responsibility for policy terms and insured-benefit decisions. Route Services operates the directory and routing tools
 under an intra-group service agreement.


 End of record • PAL-SRC-001 • Coverage Labs simulation archive




FICTIONAL SIMULATION MATERIAL                                                                            PAL-SRC-001 • PAGE 3

PALISADE / CIVIC ROUTE DOSSIER




 PALISADE / FICTIONAL TRAINING RECORD


 Regional Route Directory — Methodology and
             Snapshot Q3 2026
 PAL-SRC-005 • Methodology / dataset note • Issued 2026-10-03

 Purpose in this simulation: Explains the denominator behind the 94% directory coverage claim and its
 exclusions.


 DOCUMENT CONTROL
 This document is invented for Coverage Labs. It does not describe a real insurer, regulator, provider, person or event. Its
 contents are evidence only within the fictional Palisade investigation.



 01 / Definition
 A “route present” means that at least one provider record is associated with a care category and region in the directory at
 the snapshot date. The measure is a presence indicator, not a capacity or appointment indicator.

 02 / Denominator
 The Q3 snapshot contains 12 regions and 8 care categories, producing 96 region/category combinations. Ninety of those
 combinations contain at least one provider record: 90/96 = 93.75%, rounded to 94%.




FICTIONAL SIMULATION MATERIAL                                                                            PAL-SRC-005 • PAGE 1
 PALISADE / CIVIC ROUTE DOSSIER




 03 / Exclusions
 The calculation excludes duplicate provider records, records marked “temporarily unavailable” and categories not
 included in the eight-category directory taxonomy. The methodology does not establish whether the remaining records
 are accepting new patients.

 04 / Freshness
 The snapshot was compiled from provider files received by 15 September 2026. Two providers submitted files more than
 45 days before the snapshot. No independent confirmation of current capacity is attached.




FICTIONAL SIMULATION MATERIAL                                                                       PAL-SRC-005 • PAGE 2
 PALISADE / CIVIC ROUTE DOSSIER




 05 / Interpretation
 The report cautions that route presence should not be described as appointment availability, travel convenience, clinical
 suitability or guaranteed access. Those outcomes require separate measures.


 End of record • PAL-SRC-005 • Coverage Labs simulation archive




FICTIONAL SIMULATION MATERIAL                                                                           PAL-SRC-005 • PAGE 3

                     Office
 PAL-SRC-009 • Independent oversight review • Issued 2026-11-02

 Purpose in this simulation: Challenges interpretation of route presence and documents data limitations without
 establishing all member outcomes.


 DOCUMENT CONTROL
 This document is invented for Coverage Labs. It does not describe a real insurer, regulator, provider, person or event. Its
 contents are evidence only within the fictional Palisade investigation.



 01 / Mandate
 The fictional Waypoint Audit Office reviewed directory methodology, a sample of update logs and selected referral
 records. It did not conduct a clinical quality review or a population-wide member survey.

 02 / Finding 1
 The 94% route-presence figure is arithmetically reproducible from the supplied Q3 snapshot. The measure does not
 demonstrate that providers were accepting referrals or able to offer timely appointments.

 The audit could not reconcile all 14% of records lacking a confirmed refresh date to a current provider confirmation. It
 recommends publishing data-freshness indicators and separating directory presence from capacity.

entries.title: README.md
entries.body:
# Fictional Dutch Health Insurance Research Lab - Expanded Edition 2027

> **Closed fictional research simulation.** Every company, person, policy, institution, bank, newspaper, register, price, source and event is invented. Nothing in this lab should be used for an actual insurance decision.

## Three distinct organisations

- **Noordlicht Zorg** - Y2K cyber-goth / Windows 7 Aero desktop. Explore its history and member governance through a chaotic visual archive.
- **Rivierzorg Direct** - turquoise liquid-glass / PS3 XMB-inspired interface. Follow system architecture, network exports and service telemetry.
- **Kompas Coöperatieve Zorg** - warm red-brown Windows 8 Metro tiles. Explore household eligibility, cooperative membership and regional family support.

## What's expanded

Each company now has an expanded identity, a multi-event corporate history, three fictional policy products, a finished parent dossier, finished provider dossier, finished policy dossier, claim register, source register, evidence desk, open questions, HTML research pages, wiki and a redesigned company website. Each company has ten source PDFs (five original, five new) and company-specific data appendices.

The external simulated institutions and newsroom provide a different class of evidence: corporate registration, filing acknowledgements, supervision themes, bank financing and journalism. They are not real government or financial entities.

## Start here

1. Open `../index.html` for the Coverage Lab portal.
2. Use the Academy hypothesis ledger to manage competing explanations, source gaps and falsifiers. The former standalone case area has been retired; its competing-explanations method is now part of the Academy.
3. Explore one company at a time using its website, wiki and research desk.
4. Follow source IDs from the dossier to its source PDF.
5. Keep a record of what is supported, partly supported, disputed or unknown.

## The hidden details

There are deliberate cross-document inconsistencies, narrow definitions and shared-service hints. Answers are not shown in public-facing pages. The facilitator answer key is stored separately in `FACILITATOR_ONLY/ANSWER_KEY.md`; do not open it until you have completed the casework.

## Suggested research rule

Do not assume that a marketing label proves an operational fact. Do not assume a percentage is comparable just because it is expressed as a percentage. Do not assume a household, insured person, member and voting member are the same person category.


## Additional V0.1.4 exam world

**Palisade Civic Health Group** is a separate fictional exam company with a 1978 European airport-wayfinding visual identity. Its independent case PA-014 investigates the phrase “Every Region, Within Reach?” through eleven three-page source records. The source ecosystem adds Atlas Registry and Waypoint Audit Office as fictional institutional portals. Its current visual palette is witchy pastel sage green, lilac and purple-goth (deep aubergine, goth purple, soft violet, mint and ghost lilac), replacing the original ultramarine/orange/butter scheme. All Palisade material is simulation-only and must not be treated as real-world Dutch insurance information.

# Rivierzorg Direct - Evidence Desk

> The registers are the structured research layer. The original source PDFs remain the evidence objects. Status and confidence are distinct fields.

## Claim register quick view

| Claim ID | Topic | Evidence status | Confidence | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLM-01 | Legal identity | Supported | High | Annual report and registry identity records establish the fictional legal names. |
| CLM-02 | Policy terms | Supported | High | Policy guide describes the basis; actual claim-level outcomes are not modelled. |
| CLM-03 | Hospital network | Supported | High | Network annex defines the denominator; capacity and waiting time remain unknown. |
| CLM-04 | Customer service | Disputed | High | The source definitions, numerators and denominators differ materially. |
| CLM-05 | Outsourcing | Partly supported | Medium | Company schedule/technical or board appendix plus supplier register; complete data-processing terms are not public. |
| CLM-06 | Practical access | Unknown | High | No source provides a complete patient-level waiting-time distribution. |
| CLM-07 | Claims automation | Disputed | High | Metric note excludes incomplete, pending-document and manual-review cases. |
| CLM-08 | Platform resilience | Disputed | High | Incident report says routine app claims continued while document cases queued. |

## Evidence status vocabulary

- **Supported:** the cited fictional source directly supports the bounded claim.
- **Partly supported:** the source supports only part of the claim, or a key document is missing.
- **Disputed:** available sources conflict with the wording or interpretation.
- **Unknown:** the source pack cannot establish the claim.
- **Outdated:** a newer source supersedes the evidence.

## Confidence vocabulary

Confidence describes how confidently the research team has interpreted the available evidence. It is not the same as the evidence status. A disputed conclusion may have High confidence if the source clearly disproves the broad claim.

## Source traceability rule

Use the `source_id` as the stable identifier. Record a page or section in the claim's supporting-source list. Preserve limitations and publication / verification dates. A source being official within the fiction does not make its claims independently verified.

## Registers

- `Claims_Register.csv` - atomic claims and assessments.
- `Sources_Register.csv` - source identity, dates, type, local file and limitations.
- `Open_Questions.md` - unresolved research tasks.

| 2026 | A service interruption delays a subset of document-dependent reimbursements; the group reports recovery within two working days. |
| 2027 | The basic premium remains the lowest in this scenario, alongside the lowest non-contracted reimbursement rate. |


History is reconstructed from the fictional annual report, meeting records and website captures. It is a timeline of published claims, not a verified account of real-world events. [SRC01, SRC05, SRC06]

## 4. Ownership, control and group structure

The annual report describes the group as a privately held company. That label needs to be separated from the voting and procurement rules. The shareholder record and management disclosures do not establish public ownership or member voting rights. [SRC01, SRC06]

**Research finding:** legal ownership, governance participation, operational control and service-provider relationships are four separate questions. Do not treat the corporate group chart as complete until filed ownership, board appointments and contracts are checked.

## 5. Business model and financial profile

- Fictional insured population: 325,000 [SRC01]
- Scenario market share: 4.1% (scenario estimate) [SRC01]
- Basic premium: €145.50 monthly / €1,746.00 annually [SRC02]
- Business model: A private digital-first group that treats health insurance like a connected service layer. It is fast at routine digital transactions; the difficult questions begin where the preferred network, external care and automated exceptions meet.
- Financial reporting: the annual report provides group-level premium and expense lines but the public pack does not include a full independent audit opinion or a claim-level profitability reconciliation. [SRC01]

**Do not infer:** premium level alone does not show solvency, efficiency, claims adequacy, care quality or corporate responsibility.

## 6. Outsourcing and third-party dependencies

The document set contains a reference to Kade Data & Dossier B.V. in the service chain. Noordlicht's schedule identifies document intake and first-line file preparation; Rivierzorg's technical architecture shows a Kade Relay exception route; Kompas's board appendix contains supplier code `KDD-04` while redacting the supplier name. [SRC10]

**Evidence status:** Partly supported. The records indicate an administrative service relationship, but the full signed contract, processing agreement, subcontractor register, data-location schedule and tested exit plan are not in the public pack. No conclusion about misconduct or unlawful processing is supported.

## 7. Governance and accountability

| Topic | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Executive responsibility | Board remains responsible for insurer and policy decisions | Supported by scenario annual report |
| Member / shareholder influence | Participation depends on formal legal status and voting rules | Partly supported |
| Procurement oversight | Public records show board-level control, not direct insured-member approval | Supported in available minutes |
| Independent audit | A complete independent audit pack is not included | Unknown |
| Remuneration and conflicts | Summary disclosure only | Partly supported |

## 8. Corporate responsibility

The company's public values page refers to affordability, responsible purchasing and access. The available fictional source pack does not independently test investment exclusions, financed emissions, lobbying, labour standards, executive pay ratios or supplier working conditions. Those topics remain **Unknown**, not negative findings. [SRC01, SRC05]

## 9. Public reputation and complaints

Published complaint/service figures are not comparable across the three insurers. The 78% figure counts hospital addresses with an active status in the 2027 directory export. It does not measure appointment capacity, specialties, treatment-level contracts or referral acceptance. The complaints rate counts tagged support tickets per active digital account, not only formal complaints. [SRC04, SRC08, SRC09]

**Finding:** the headline rates should be reported with their definitions, populations and exclusions. A ranking based on `3.8`, `5.6` and `3.1` alone would be unsound.

## 10. Parent-group assessment summary

| Dimension | Finding | Evidence status | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legal identity | Parent and insurer entities are named in the fictional records | Supported | High |
| Ownership and control | More detail needed on effective control and service-provider influence | Partly supported | Medium |
| Financial transparency | Aggregate figures present; complete independent pack absent | Partly supported | Medium |
| Outsourcing | Administrative relationship indicated; full agreement absent | Partly supported | Medium |
| Governance influence | Formal structures described; practical member influence differs | Partly supported | Medium |
| Corporate responsibility | Marketing commitments exist; implementation evidence is missing | Unknown | Unknown |

No composite score is assigned. The assessment is a source-led summary, not a recommendation.

## 11. Unresolved questions

1. Obtain the full signed service contract and processing annex for Kade Data & Dossier B.V.
2. Identify all subcontractors, data locations, incident responsibilities and exit arrangements.
3. Obtain the complete audited financial statements and notes on related-party transactions.
4. Compare voting eligibility with the number of insured persons and household members.
5. Obtain independent complaints data using a common definition.
6. Verify whether published care-access claims match provider-level contracts and appointment capacity.

## 12. Source index

See `Sources_Register.csv` for source metadata and exact local PDF paths. Key supporting records: SRC01 annual report; SRC06 governance record; SRC08 service/metric record; SRC09 simulated KRO register extract; SRC10 service/outsourcing schedule.

# Rivierzorg Direct - Policy Dossier / Insurance Year 2027

> **FICTIONAL SIMULATION ONLY.** All prices, packages and terms below are invented for research practice. They are not real policy terms, real Dutch statutory benefits, or a substitute for an insurer's official contract.

**Provider:** Rivierzorg Verzekeringen N.V.  
**Parent group:** Riviergroep N.V.  
**Policy year:** 2027  
**Verification date:** 17 November 2026  
**Primary source:** `RIVIERZORG-SRC-002`

## Product catalogue

### Rivier Basis Select

**Basic insurance | €145.50 / month**

- Budget naturapolis; annual basic premium €1,746.00.
- Non-contracted care: 60% of the average contracted tariff subject to service-specific maximum amounts.
- Voluntary deductible options in this exercise: up to €885 on top of the assumed €385 scenario deductible.
- The 78% network headline measures hospital addresses marked active in a directory snapshot, not contracted specialties or available appointments.

Source: RIVIERZORG-SRC-002 and RIVIERZORG-SRC-007.

### Rivier Start

**Supplementary | €15.95 / month**

- 6 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €250 per policy year.
- Some complex dental treatments have a 12-month waiting period.
- App-based claims are supported; paper submission remains available for exceptions.

Source: RIVIERZORG-SRC-002.

### Rivier Stroom

**Supplementary | €27.50 / month**

- 9 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €400 per policy year.
- Selected optical contribution up to €100 every two calendar years.
- Treatment at non-preferred supplementary providers may receive no benefit unless pre-authorised.

Source: RIVIERZORG-SRC-002.


## Calculation notes

- Monthly premium multiplied by twelve gives the annual basic premium only; add-on costs are separate.
- The assumed €385 deductible is a scenario parameter and should not be carried over into real-world advice.
- Non-contracted reimbursement percentages use a fictional insurer-defined tariff basis. They do not mean the same percentage of an invoice is paid.
- Annual caps are per policy year unless the wording says otherwise.
- Supplementary benefits do not alter the basic-policy contract or create unlimited provider choice.

## Exclusions and conditions to investigate

1. Provider contract and legal entity at the exact treatment location.
2. Whether an annual maximum is per insured person, household, treatment type or policy.
3. Prior authorisation and referral conditions.
4. Waiting periods and exclusions for planned or pre-existing treatment.
5. Treatment definitions, clinical criteria and approved codes.
6. Non-contracted care caps, maximum tariffs and administrative fees.
7. Whether unused sessions roll over and whether multiple packages can be combined.

## Research status

This is a finished training dossier for the supplied source pack. It is not a complete real-world policy audit. Unknown items remain unknown; do not infer them from marketing copy or from the package name.

# Rivierzorg Direct - Insurance Provider Research Dossier

> **FICTIONAL SIMULATION.** This completed training example does not describe a real insurance provider, contract or Dutch healthcare entitlement.

**Dossier status:** Completed example / policy and provider-access focus  
**Verification date:** 17 November 2026  
**Public brand:** Rivierzorg Direct  
**Legal insurer:** Rivierzorg Verzekeringen N.V.  
**Parent group:** Riviergroep N.V.  
**Basic policy:** Rivier Basis Select  
**Product type:** Budget naturapolis

## 1. Identity and legal responsibility

The brand is the customer-facing identity. The fictional policy guide names `Rivierzorg Verzekeringen N.V.` as the insurer, and the annual report identifies `Riviergroep N.V.` as the parent group. These are separate legal and commercial layers. [SRC01, SRC02]

## 2. Basic policy and price

| Field | Scenario value |
|---|---|
| Policy | Rivier Basis Select |
| Type | Budget naturapolis |
| Monthly premium | €145.50 |
| Annual premium | €1,746.00 |
| Non-contracted care | 60% of the insurer-defined average contracted tariff; additional maximum reimbursement amounts apply |
| Assumed deductible | €385 scenario parameter; voluntary options up to €885 |
| Hospital network headline | 78% |

The deductible is a fictional scenario parameter. It is not intended as a statement of the actual statutory deductible for any real policy year. Reimbursement is based on the insurer-defined tariff and may be affected by a cap, exclusion, authorisation requirement, provider type or treatment code. [SRC02]

## 3. Supplementary packages

### Rivier Start

**Supplementary - €15.95 / month**

- 6 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €250 per policy year.
- Some complex dental treatments have a 12-month waiting period.
- App-based claims are supported; paper submission remains available for exceptions.

Source: RIVIERZORG-SRC-002.

### Rivier Stroom

**Supplementary - €27.50 / month**

- 9 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €400 per policy year.
- Selected optical contribution up to €100 every two calendar years.
- Treatment at non-preferred supplementary providers may receive no benefit unless pre-authorised.

Source: RIVIERZORG-SRC-002.


## 4. Provider choice and network access

Headline network figure: **78%**. The 78% figure counts hospital addresses with an active status in the 2027 directory export. It does not measure appointment capacity, specialties, treatment-level contracts or referral acceptance. The complaints rate counts tagged support tickets per active digital account, not only formal complaints. [SRC03, SRC07/SRC08]

The percentage must be read as an administrative directory indicator. It does not establish availability for a specific provider, site, specialty, date or patient pathway. A complete access check would need the exact legal entity, location, service code, contract period, referral pathway, capacity and waiting time.

## 5. Care-specific evidence

| Care area | Published description | Evidence limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Mental healthcare | Digital intake and online therapy are readily available; face-to-face contracted options are thinner in rural areas. Wait estimates are supplied by provider, not independently measured. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Gender-affirming healthcare | No dedicated in-house pathway. Referrals are made to external contracted providers; non-contracted specialist care may leave substantial out-of-pocket costs. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Women's healthcare | Standard maternity and medically necessary gynaecological care through the preferred network; fewer independent clinics are listed in northern and rural areas. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Disability and rehabilitation | Medical aids are handled through selected suppliers; claims are digital-first and named case management is limited. | Company report / not an access guarantee |
| Physiotherapy and dental | Start includes 6 sessions and 75% dental up to €250; major dental treatments may have a 12-month waiting period. | Company report / not an access guarantee |

## 6. Customer service and complaints

The published complaint/service figure is **5.6 / 1,000**. The 78% figure counts hospital addresses with an active status in the 2027 directory export. It does not measure appointment capacity, specialties, treatment-level contracts or referral acceptance. The complaints rate counts tagged support tickets per active digital account, not only formal complaints. [SRC04, SRC09]

The complaint measure is not directly comparable with the other companies. The numerator and denominator differ: tagged digital support tickets divided by active digital accounts; app and login issues are included. Report this metric with that definition, or omit it from a cross-company ranking.

## 7. Practical-access checklist

For a real or simulated treatment scenario, record:

1. Exact treatment and service code.
2. Named provider and contracting legal entity.
3. Treatment location and policy-year contract status.
4. Referral, clinical indication and prior-authorisation conditions.
5. Reimbursement basis, maximum tariff, annual cap and likely patient share.
6. Current waiting-time information and continuity arrangements.
7. Travel, accessibility, language and support needs.

## 8. Claim-level assessment

| Claim | Status | Confidence | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brand / legal insurer relationship | Supported | High | Named in policy guide and annual report |
| Published premium and benefit summary | Supported | High | Stated in fictional policy guide; full terms still matter |
| Practical availability of all advertised pathways | Unknown | Medium | No patient-level capacity and waiting-time dataset |
| Network headline as a measure of access | Disputed | High | Source denominator does not measure specialty or appointments |
| Cross-company complaint ranking | Disputed | High | Definitions and denominators differ |

## 9. Strengths, constraints and unresolved matters

**Potential strengths**
- Low premium and fast routine digital claims.

**Potential constraints**
- Narrower preferred network, lower reimbursement and limited in-person navigation.

**Still unknown**
- Individual provider contracts and actual appointment capacity.
- Complete policy wording and claim-level examples.
- Independent customer-outcome evidence.
- Full data-processing and subcontractor arrangements.

## 10. Conclusion

Rivierzorg Direct presents a distinct policy and service proposition in this fictional scenario. A suitability conclusion depends on a person's location, provider, treatment needs, policy combination and risk tolerance. No overall recommendation or score is assigned.

## Sources

See `Sources_Register.csv`. Start with SRC02 (policy), SRC03 (network), SRC04 (service), and company-specific SRC06-SRC10 records. All sources are fictional training artefacts.

# Rivierzorg Direct - Fictional Company Wiki

> **FICTIONAL SIMULATION.** This is a secondary training article. The organisation, people, policies, prices, documents, events and figures are invented. It is not a real company, insurer, policy or legal record.

## Overview

A private digital-first group that treats health insurance like a connected service layer. It is fast at routine digital transactions; the difficult questions begin where the preferred network, external care and automated exceptions meet.

## Corporate profile

- **Parent group:** Riviergroep N.V.
- **Legal insurer:** Rivierzorg Verzekeringen N.V.
- **Public brand:** Rivierzorg Direct
- **Registered office (scenario):** Utrecht
- **Founded (scenario):** 2018
- **Insured population:** 325,000
- **Scenario market share:** 4.1% (scenario estimate)
- **Company model:** Privately held digital-first group

## History

- **2018:** Riviergroep is founded by a technology-led investment consortium to build a lower-cost digital insurer.
- **2019:** Rivierzorg launches a budget naturapolis supported by an app-first claims engine.
- **2020:** A preferred-provider network replaces the broad open network used in the pilot.
- **2022:** The group rolls out FlowCore, an automated authorisation and claims-routing platform.
- **2025:** The platform is connected to a third-party case and document relay for exceptions and manual review.
- **2026:** A service interruption delays a subset of document-dependent reimbursements; the group reports recovery within two working days.
- **2027:** The basic premium remains the lowest in this scenario, alongside the lowest non-contracted reimbursement rate.

## Insurance products

### Rivier Basis Select

**Basic insurance - €145.50 / month**
- Budget naturapolis; annual basic premium €1,746.00.
- Non-contracted care: 60% of the average contracted tariff subject to service-specific maximum amounts.
- Voluntary deductible options in this exercise: up to €885 on top of the assumed €385 scenario deductible.
- The 78% network headline measures hospital addresses marked active in a directory snapshot, not contracted specialties or available appointments.
### Rivier Start

**Supplementary - €15.95 / month**
- 6 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €250 per policy year.
- Some complex dental treatments have a 12-month waiting period.
- App-based claims are supported; paper submission remains available for exceptions.
### Rivier Stroom

**Supplementary - €27.50 / month**
- 9 physiotherapy sessions per policy year.
- Adult dental: 75% up to €400 per policy year.
- Selected optical contribution up to €100 every two calendar years.
- Treatment at non-preferred supplementary providers may receive no benefit unless pre-authorised.

## Care access

- **Mental healthcare:** Digital intake and online therapy are readily available; face-to-face contracted options are thinner in rural areas. Wait estimates are supplied by provider, not independently measured.
- **Gender-affirming healthcare:** No dedicated in-house pathway. Referrals are made to external contracted providers; non-contracted specialist care may leave substantial out-of-pocket costs.
- **Women's healthcare:** Standard maternity and medically necessary gynaecological care through the preferred network; fewer independent clinics are listed in northern and rural areas.
- **Disability and rehabilitation:** Medical aids are handled through selected suppliers; claims are digital-first and named case management is limited.
- **Physiotherapy and dental:** Start includes 6 sessions and 75% dental up to €250; major dental treatments may have a 12-month waiting period.

## Customer service and public metrics

- **Headline premium:** €145.50 monthly.
- **Hospital network headline:** 78%.
- **Published complaints/service rate:** 5.6 / 1,000.

These measures are not directly comparable across the three fictional companies. Their numerators, denominators, periods and exclusions differ. The network figures describe administrative directory measures, not appointment access or clinical capacity.

## Governance, service partners and unresolved questions

The platform architecture describes an external exception route and a separate document relay. The service metrics exclude cases that require manual documents or review.

The source pack contains references to a shared administrative service environment. A service relationship is not proof of ownership, unlawful processing, shared claim decisions or common corporate control. The full contract, processing annex, subcontractor list and operational audit are not available.

## Primary sources

See `Sources_Register.csv` and the `Sources/` folder. The wiki is not a substitute for the policy guide, corporate report, network annex, governance records or supplier schedule.

## Research links

- [Research overview](../research/overview.html)
- [Parent group dossier](../research/Parent_Research.md)
- [Provider dossier](../research/Provider_Research.md)
- [Policy dossier](../research/Policy_Research.md)
- [Evidence desk](../research/Evidence_Desk.md)

## Editorial note

Check every material statement against the linked fictional primary source. Preserve evidence status, confidence and source limitations separately. All material is fictional training content.

entries.title: Solstice Tutorial — Coverage Labs
entries.body: Solstice Tutorial — Coverage Labs ☼ SOLSTICE / GUIDED INVESTIGATION COVERAGE LABS HOME ↗ COMPANY SITE ↗ PROVISIONAL COMPANY IDENTITY · V0.1.2 THE 96% QUESTION. Nine practical modules. One fictional insurer and its surrounding ecosystem. Your job is to discover what the bright promise actually measures — and what it leaves unanswered. Everything in this learning environment is invented. No real insurer, policy, person or institution is represented. YOUR INVESTIGATION 0 of 9 modules complete 01 / Understand the assignment Module 1 02 / Understand the organisation Module 2 03 / Deconstruct claims Module 3 04 / Find and evaluate sources Module 4 05 / Build the evidence trail Module 5 06 / Assess findings Module 6 07 / Write the investigation Module 7 08 / Follow incentives Module 8 09 / Test explanations Module 9 Progress is saved locally in this browser. It is not synced or backed up. CASE BRIEF Solstice Cover publicly states that 96% of its members can reach a listed care partner within 30 minutes. Test the statement. Do not assume that a listed provider is accepting patients or that geographic proximity equals practical access. MODULE 01 / 09 Understand the assignment Learning objective: Turn the brief into an investigation question. YOUR ASSIGNMENT What does “96% can reach a listed care partner within 30 minutes” actually promise? Separate the question, the company claim and a finding. Useful starting point: Solstice research desk · Company wiki · Public website Check your reasoning Which is a testable claim? Solstice is trustworthy 96% of members can reach a listed partner within 30 minutes Investigate Solstice Check answer Your field note Mark module complete Next module → MODULE 02 / 09 Understand the organisation Learning objective: Map who owns, provides and performs the work. YOUR ASSIGNMENT Use the wiki and SOL-SRC-001 / SOL-SRC-004. Identify the parent, risk-bearing provider and service operator. Useful starting point: Solstice research desk · Company wiki · Public website Check your reasoning Who is named as the risk-bearing provider? Solstice Mutual Holdings U.A. Solstice Zorg N.V. Dayglow Member Services B.V. Check answer Your field note Mark module complete Next module → MODULE 03 / 09 Deconstruct claims Learning objective: Break broad promises into propositions that evidence can test. YOUR ASSIGNMENT Work with CLM-01, CLM-02 and CLM-03. For each, identify a measurable proposition and what evidence would be needed. Useful starting point: Solstice research desk · Company wiki · Public website Check your reasoning What is essential to test the 96% figure? The colour of the website Its denominator and definition of “reach” The CEO biography Check answer Your field note Mark module complete Next module → MODULE 04 / 09 Find and evaluate sources Learning objective: Choose sources for the question they can actually answer. YOUR ASSIGNMENT Open all five source PDFs from the research desk. Classify each as primary or secondary and assess relevance, authority, date and limitations. Useful starting point: Solstice research desk · Company wiki · Public website Check your reasoning Which source defines the calculation behind 96%? SOL-SRC-001 SOL-SRC-002 SOL-SRC-005 Check answer Your field note Mark module complete Next module → MODULE 05 / 09 Build the evidence trail Learning objective: Connect each claim to supporting, qualifying and contradictory evidence. YOUR ASSIGNMENT Use SOL-SRC-002 and SOL-SRC-005. Record direct evidence separately from inference. Useful starting point: Solstice research desk · Company wiki · Public website Check your reasoning What does SOL-SRC-005 establish? Nationally, exactly one-third of providers are inaccessible Some sampled listed locations were not accepting patients; the sample is not representative The 96% calculation is fraudulent Check answer Your field note Mark module complete Next module → MODULE 06 / 09 Assess findings Learning objective: Choose evidence status and confidence independently. YOUR ASSIGNMENT Assess CLM-01. Then choose a confidence level based on source quality, consistency and completeness. Useful starting point: Solstice research desk · Company wiki · Public website Check your reasoning The 96% figure measures directory proximity, not appointment access. Best status for the broad practical-access claim? Supported Partly supported Disputed Unknown Outdated Check answer Your field note Mark module complete Next module → MODULE 07 / 09 Write the investigation Learning objective: Turn the evidence trail into a concise, transparent report. YOUR ASSIGNMENT Complete the final brief: profile the group, state the findings, cite source IDs and preserve unresolved questions. Useful starting point: Solstice research desk · Company wiki · Public website Check your reasoning Which sentence is most defensible? Solstice guarantees access for 96% of members. The 96% metric measures proximity to active directory listings; it does not establish appointment availability. Solstice has no accessible care. Check answer Your field note Mark module complete Next module → MODULE 08 / 09 Follow incentives, not assumptions Learning objective: Identify who benefits from a decision without treating motive as proof of misconduct. YOUR ASSIGNMENT Review the fictional annual strategy, investor note and procurement extracts. Identify one financial or operational incentive behind the 96% proximity metric or the provider-network design. Then identify an alternative explanation. Useful starting point: Solstice research desk · VINDR: capital allocation · VINDR sponsored results Check your reasoning A supplier contract creates a financial incentive. What does that establish by itself? That the supplier controlled the insurer's decisions That a commercial relationship exists; its influence and consequences need separate evidence That a member was denied care Check answer Your field note Mark module complete Next module → MODULE 09 / 09 Keep competing explanations alive Learning objective: Build a hypothesis ledger and identify evidence that could falsify your preferred explanation. YOUR ASSIGNMENT Consider three explanations: ordinary administrative consolidation; shared commercial infrastructure; or fragmented systems and changing suppliers. For each, list supporting evidence, contradictory evidence and the missing record that would distinguish it. Useful starting point: Institutions directory · VINDR: platform records · Academy hypothesis ledger Check your reasoning Which is the strongest next step when two explanations fit the same records? Choose the most dramatic explanation Ignore the contradiction and write the conclusion Identify a discriminating record or test that could separate the explanations Check answer Your field note Mark module complete Finish investigation Keep your reasoning inspectable. A correct multiple-choice answer is only a checkpoint; your written field notes are where the investigation becomes yours.

It recommends service maps, tested exit plans and member-level incident reporting. It is a sector-level note, not a finding against a named insurer. The NZT follow-up questionnaire distinguishes a documented exit plan from evidence that the plan was tested. Nine of twelve fictional organisations returned a completed follow-up; the aggregate figures are self-reported and the sample is not representative. To investigate a specific arrangement, seek the contract, service schedule, operational process map, escalation matrix and evidence of actual performance. Do not infer decision-making responsibility from a supplier name alone.
