entries.title: V0.1.3 — Worked Example | Coverage Labs
entries.body: V0.1.3 — Worked Example | Coverage Labs COVERAGE LABS / FREQ HOME COMPANY WIKI RESEARCH DESK V0.1.3 / WORKED EXAMPLE / CASE FE-013 SIMULATION SYSTEM ONLINE THE COMPLETE INVESTIGATION / FREQUENCY HEALTH GROUP ONE CALL. ONE ANSWER? Explore a finished investigation from assignment to final report. Follow the evidence trail, inspect the documents and see how a defensible conclusion is built without pretending the evidence says more than it does. Central question Does Frequency's 88% first-contact resolution figure show that 88% of member problems were solved without further contact? FREQUENCY MEDIA GUIDE ● ACTIVE CASE CHANNELS SELECT A FILE TO EXPLORE 01 CLAIMS 09 SOURCES 04 FINDINGS CASE STATUS: COMPLETED WITH OPEN QUESTIONS INVESTIGATION MENU 01 / ASSIGNMENT 02 / ENTITY MAP 03 / CLAIMS 04 / SOURCE LIBRARY 05 / EVIDENCE TRAIL 06 / ASSESSMENTS 07 / FINAL REPORT 08 / YOUR WORKSPACE CASE COMPLETION 0 of 8 sections reviewed 01 / ASSIGNMENT What are we trying to establish? Frequency Health Group publicly says that 88% of eligible service contacts were resolved at first contact in Q4 2026. Its slogan is “One call. One answer.” The investigation must test whether the metric supports the broader impression that a member's issue is resolved in one interaction. Scope Identify the entities involved in insurance decisions, member service and network coordination. Determine exactly how the 88% figure is calculated. Test whether closure of an interaction is equivalent to resolution of a member issue. Assess the separate claim about network slot visibility. State what can be concluded, what remains unknown and what evidence would improve the investigation. Important distinction: A question identifies what you want to know. A claim is a proposition someone makes. A finding is what your evidence supports after testing that proposition. Primary question: What does the 88% measure establish—and what does it not establish? MARK SECTION REVIEWED START HERE Read the Frequency public website , then compare its claims with the company wiki and research desk . 02 / ENTITY MAP One brand, several entities Entity Relationship Responsibility established by records Frequency Health Group U.A. Parent cooperative Group strategy and governance; parent of Zorg and Connect in register extract. Frequency Zorg N.V. Wholly owned provider subsidiary Insurance provider; retains policy interpretation, coverage decisions and formal complaint determinations. Frequency Connect B.V. Wholly owned service subsidiary First-line contact, identity checks, intake, triage and routing. Frequency Network B.V. Relationship not fully established in register extract Provider directory and data-feed coordination; shareholding not recorded in extract. The shared brand is not a legal entity map. The register establishes ownership links for two subsidiaries; the agreement establishes specified service responsibilities; neither source alone proves actual performance. Finding: Frequency is a group of distinct entities presenting a coordinated brand. The available record does not establish that one legal entity performs every function. MARK SECTION REVIEWED 03 / CLAIM DECONSTRUCTION Translate the slogans into testable propositions ID Public wording Testable proposition What evidence is needed? CLM-01 88% resolved at first contact 88% of member issues ended without repeat contact or further action. Metric definition, denominator, linked repeat contacts and case outcomes. CLM-02 One call, one answer A member can complete the relevant service journey in one contact. Service agreement, transfer records, member journeys and outcome records. CLM-03 92% of locations show a slot within 14 days 92% of members can obtain a suitable appointment within 14 days. Slot methodology, live booking confirmation, specialty suitability and referral outcomes. CLM-04 One integrated service One legal entity controls all service and decision responsibilities. Entity register, service agreements, governance and operational evidence. A good testable proposition is narrower than a slogan. It identifies the unit being measured, the time period and the outcome that would count as success. MARK SECTION REVIEWED 04 / SOURCE LIBRARY Nine records, different evidential jobs Open the source itself. The notes below explain what it can establish and where its limits begin. FREQ-SRC-001 Annual Signal Report 2026 ↗ Frequency Health Group — corporate publication. Limitation: Self-published group narrative; does not establish operational performance. FREQ-SRC-002 Entity Register Extract ↗ Fictional Civic Registry — simulated register extract. Limitation: Register extract is limited to the listed entities and filing dates; it does not establish day-to-day practice. FREQ-SRC-003 Member Services Agreement — Extract ↗ Frequency Zorg N.V. and Frequency Connect B.V. — executed fictional agreement. Limitation: Only selected clauses are reproduced; schedules, service-level annexes and data processing terms are absent. FREQ-SRC-004 TUNE KPI Methodology v3.2 ↗ Frequency Connect B.V. — internal metric specification. Limitation: Internal methodology is a strong source for the reported calculation, but it is not an independent audit of source data. FREQ-SRC-005 Q4 Service Performance Dashboard ↗ Frequency Connect B.V. — internal operational report. Limitation: Aggregated dashboard; no member-level linkage or underlying interaction export supplied. FREQ-SRC-006 Repeat Contact Review — Sample Ledger ↗ Frequency Quality Office — fictional internal sample. Limitation: Convenience sample of 40 cases; not random and not suitable for estimating a population rate. FREQ-SRC-007 Network Slot Availability Bulletin ↗ Frequency Network B.V. — fictional provider network report. Limitation: Snapshot of listed slot data; does not independently verify appointment booking or clinical suitability. FREQ-SRC-008 Board Risk Note 04/27 ↗ Frequency Health Group U.A. — confidential fictional board extract. Limitation: Partial board note; context and subsequent actions are not included. FREQ-SRC-009 The Queue Is Not the Outcome ↗ The Signal Desk — independent fictional reporting. Limitation: Secondary reporting based on interviews and a small document sample; not a representative survey. Primary does not mean unlimited. A corporate annual report is primary evidence of what the company said; the internal methodology is primary evidence of how it defined the metric; neither independently audits whether the member's issue was solved. Also inspect the company website , wiki and independent fictional Signal Desk report . MARK SECTION REVIEWED 05 / EVIDENCE TRAIL Connect each claim to the record Claim Supporting / confirming evidence Qualifying / contradictory evidence What remains unknown CLM-01 / 88% FCR SRC-004 defines FCR; SRC-005 reproduces 88.0% under that method. SRC-003 permits transfer/next-step closure; SRC-006 identifies repeat journeys; SRC-008 recognises missing end-to-end evidence; SRC-009 corroborates interpretation. Population-level member issue resolution rate; repeat contact rate across all channels. CLM-02 / one call SRC-001 describes shared service experience. SRC-003 allocates first-line work and final decisions to different entities; SRC-006 gives examples of further member action. How often members complete a full issue in one interaction. CLM-03 / 92% slots SRC-001 states the headline; SRC-007 shows 1,693/1,840 locations with a slot visible. SRC-007 does not confirm live availability, suitability or booking; 126 feeds were late. Actual member appointment access within 14 days. CLM-04 / integrated group SRC-002 establishes some ownership links; SRC-003 establishes contractual division of tasks. Distinct legal entities retain different responsibilities; ownership of Network not shown in extract. Complete ownership and full operational accountability, including missing schedules. Direct evidence versus inference Direct evidence: TUNE's definition says an interaction may be marked resolved after a transfer is accepted. Inference: a member may still need further action. The sample ledger supplies examples of that possibility, but does not estimate how common it is across all members. MARK SECTION REVIEWED 06 / FINDINGS ASSESSMENT Status and confidence are separate judgements Finding Evidence status Confidence Reason 88% of eligible interactions were marked resolved at closure under TUNE v3.2. SUPPORTED HIGH Methodology and dashboard align; denominator and calculation are stated. Members generally complete full service journeys in one contact. UNKNOWN HIGH The available measures count interactions, not linked member-level outcomes; the selected sample cannot establish prevalence. The 88% figure proves 88% of member problems were solved in one contact. DISPUTED HIGH Methodology does not measure member-level outcomes; transfers can count as resolved and repeat contacts are not linked. 92% of members can obtain a suitable appointment within 14 days. PARTLY SUPPORTED HIGH 92% of listed locations show a slot in a feed; actual booking and suitability are not measured. One legal entity performs all service and decision responsibilities. DISPUTED HIGH Register and agreement identify distinct entities and allocated responsibilities. The public wording was deliberately designed to mislead. UNKNOWN HIGH Evidence identifies an overbroad impression and internal awareness of limitations, but not intent. Evidence status describes how the claim relates to the evidence. Confidence describes how sure we are that our assessment is well-founded. A disputed claim can have high-confidence assessment. MARK SECTION REVIEWED THE SIGNAL FILE / INVESTIGATIVE REPORT 013 One call. One answer? Frequency Health Group · Case FE-013 · 14 February 2027 Executive finding Frequency's reported 88% first-contact resolution figure is supported as a calculation of eligible interaction records marked RESOLVED at closure under TUNE methodology version 3.2. It does not establish that 88% of members' underlying issues were solved without repeat contact or further action. What the evidence shows The public annual report presents an 88% first-contact resolution result and uses the phrase “One call. One answer.” (FREQ-SRC-001). The internal methodology defines the numerator by interaction closure code, not by a verified member outcome. It allows some transfers and next-step instructions to be counted as RESOLVED and does not link later contacts when they carry a new interaction ID (FREQ-SRC-004). The Q4 dashboard reproduces the figure under that definition (FREQ-SRC-005). The member services agreement also permits an interaction to be marked complete after a transfer is accepted or a follow-up route is explained (FREQ-SRC-003). A selected quality sample contains journeys in which members contacted the organisation again or continued to another team after the first interaction was marked resolved (FREQ-SRC-006). Because the sample was selected from a follow-up queue, it cannot establish a population-wide failure rate. Corporate responsibility The register extract identifies Frequency Health Group U.A. as parent of Frequency Zorg N.V. and Frequency Connect B.V. (FREQ-SRC-002). The agreement assigns first-line contact and routing to Frequency Connect, while Frequency Zorg retains policy interpretation, coverage decisions and formal complaint determinations (FREQ-SRC-003). The available extract does not establish the full ownership of Frequency Network B.V. Other service claims The 92% network figure is supported as a count of listed locations with a slot visible in a data feed. It does not establish that 92% of members can book a suitable appointment within 14 days (FREQ-SRC-007). Conclusion and limits The headline metric is not shown to be arithmetically false. Its public presentation invites a broader interpretation than its technical definition supports. The available evidence does not establish deliberate deception, the actual member-level resolution rate, or the frequency of repeat contacts across the entire membership. The board note indicates that the group recognised the measurement gap and had requested further work, but the supplied record does not establish whether those actions were completed (FREQ-SRC-008). Further records required Linked member- and issue-level interaction data across telephone, chat and provider portal. Complete managed-services schedules and escalation matrix. Case outcome reconciliation and formal complaint records. Live appointment booking confirmations, feed freshness and specialty suitability data. Follow-up board minutes and evidence of revised public wording. Overall assessment: The 88% interaction-closure result is supported. The broader claim that 88% of member problems are resolved in one contact is disputed. The true member-level outcome rate remains unknown. MARK REPORT REVIEWED 08 / YOUR WORKSPACE Build your own version Use these prompts to reconstruct the investigation in your own words. Your notes are saved locally in this browser only. 1. Your company profile 2. Your strongest finding 3. A contradiction or qualification 4. Unresolved questions SAVE NOTES RESET SECTION TRACKER No account or cloud sync. Notes remain in this browser profile. COVERAGE LABS / V0.1.3 — WORKED EXAMPLE · FREQUENCY HEALTH GROUP IS ENTIRELY FICTIONAL · THE COMPLETED INVESTIGATION IS A TEACHING MODEL, NOT A REAL-WORLD FINDING.

entries.title: Investigator Academy | Coverage Labs
entries.body: Investigator Academy | Coverage Labs ← COVERAGE LABS INVESTIGATOR ACADEMY / FIELD DESK LOCAL SAVE READY FIELD SCHOOL · RESEARCH METHOD 01 Learn the method. Build the record. A course, a shared investigation workspace and six reusable company profiles. Work locally, save as you go, and export a backup whenever you like. Export all progress Import backup Install offline app Progress is stored in this browser on this device. It is not uploaded or synchronised. Clearing browser data can erase it; export backups regularly. 01 / COURSE The investigator’s toolkit 0 / 10 complete 02 / COMPANY PROFILES Six company dossiers. One method. Open a profile to record research in a consistent structure. 03 / INVESTIGATIVE METHOD Competing explanations HYPOTHESIS LEDGER Do not organise an investigation around a single theory. Keep several explanations alive, record what supports and contradicts each, and identify what would falsify them. A shared supplier, investor or workflow does not automatically imply shared control. Hypothesis A — ordinary administration Hypothesis B — commercial alignment or shared infrastructure Hypothesis C — fragmented systems, changing vendors or local exceptions What would change your mind? (falsifiers and missing records) 04 / FIELD NOTEBOOK Research notebook Questions that cut across companies Evidence requests to prioritise Ownership, financing and shareholdings Commercial incentives and possible motives Related parties and conflicts of interest Working synthesis 05 / INVESTIGATION CASEBOOK Build the case. Keep it open. LIVE WORKING FILE A casebook is not a reveal or a single theory. It is a structured record of claims, entities, timelines, competing explanations, contradictions and the next document that could change your mind. Use it across all six company worlds. 01 · The question Central investigative question Scope and boundaries 02 · The evidence ledger Claims and source IDs Contradictions and gaps 03 · Entity and motive map People, companies, ownership and money Incentives and alternative explanations 04 · The next move Priority records to obtain What would change your mind? CASEBOOK RULE Never promote a relationship into control, a correlation into causation, a company statement into an outcome, or a missing record into proof of concealment. FICTIONAL TRAINING ENVIRONMENT · LOCAL-FIRST · NOT REAL INSURANCE RESEARCH 06 / ARCHIVED CASEBOOK · RESTORED Company trails & shared case NATIVE ACADEMY WORKSPACE The archived casebook is now part of the Academy. These are working investigation briefs, not answer keys. Open the company records, follow the trail, and record what each document can and cannot establish. 01 · Noordlicht — corporate archaeology Compare member governance, legal identity, procurement and supplier paperwork. Test the difference between a member-owned description and actual decision rights. Company website ↗ · Research overview ↗ · Wiki ↗ Entity map and governance finding What is still unproven? 02 · Rivierzorg — systems investigation Follow event codes, the provider-directory data dictionary, service interruptions and the claims-speed metric. Establish what each published number actually measures. Company website ↗ · Research overview ↗ · Wiki ↗ Process and metric reconstruction Where does the metric stop being informative? 03 · Kompas — household & membership Follow a household across eligibility, family navigation and cooperative voting. Find where the public family promise meets formal categories and member rights. Company website ↗ · Research overview ↗ · Wiki ↗ Eligibility and rights matrix Exceptions and unresolved categories 04 · Shared service question — cross-company synthesis Three brands use different language and systems. Determine which relationships are evidenced, which are plausible, and which records would close the gaps. Institution directory ↗ · Search VINDR ↗ Network numbers and denominator comparison Shared administration and supplier map Confidence boundary CASEBOOK RULE A shared supplier, investor, platform or workflow does not automatically establish shared control, coordinated intent or a common outcome. Keep alternative explanations alive and identify what would falsify each one.
